migration.scope: STRUCTURAL ONLY. No new researched values. Fields awaiting cited data are null with a needs_source flag so the validator blocks on them.

gloss_class.boundary_authority: CONVENTION (BLOCKMIND), pending data. Four levels chosen so that no single value is adjacent to all others. ISO 2813:2014 defines the MEASUREMENT, not these bands; the matte<10 / semi-gloss 10-70 / gloss>70 GU convention is instrument practice, and the mirror band is required because polished metal exceeds the 0-100 GU coating scale. Real-world interlaboratory reproducibility reaches ~10 GU (Leloup et al. 2016 JCTR 13(6):941).

vhc_class.boundary_authority: CONVENTION (BLOCKMIND). Edges placed in gaps in the observed value distribution rather than at round numbers. No standard bins materials by volumetric heat capacity.
vhc_class.standard: EN ISO 10456:2007 Table 3 (source of rho and c only, not of the bands)
vhc_class.supersedes: v2.6 four-band scheme, edges 0.8/1.5/2.5, which left 32 of 107 materials within 10 percent of an edge and had an empty top band at pixel level. Old values are in v2_7_changelog.csv.

vapour_class.boundary_authority: CONVENTION (BLOCKMIND), pending data. EN ISO 10456 tabulates mu; it does not band it. Only three levels because mu interlaboratory scatter exceeds 20-30%, so finer bins would be noise. NOTE: a 3-level ordinal has a universally-adjacent middle; this is safe ONLY because scoring is quadratic-weighted kappa, under which any constant answer scores 0.

substrate_finish_class.boundaries: matte <10 GU; semi_gloss 10-70 GU; gloss >70 GU; mirror off the 0-100 coating scale (polished metal, mirrors)
substrate_finish_class.boundary_authority: CONVENTION. The 10 and 70 GU cuts are the instrument geometry selection thresholds in ISO 2813 and the MPI G-level ladder, not a normative banding of materials.
substrate_finish_class.definition: Specular gloss of the material AS MANUFACTURED, including finishes integral to its manufacture (glaze, mill finish, polish) but excluding paint, varnish, lacquer or sealer applied on site.
substrate_finish_class.replaces: legacy_reflectance_label, which conflated specular gloss with solar reflectance and disagreed with its own numeric field on 44 of 107 entries.

dropped_dimensions.emissivity_class: Considered and rejected. ESTIMATE, NOT MEASURED: the hierarchy contains no emissivity data. Using a keyword proxy over material names (bare metal vs not), roughly 100 of 107 entries would fall in high_e, an always-high_e answer would score about 0.935, and Cramer's V against the legacy reflectance label is about 0.44. Only 9 metal keys exist, split 5 bare / 4 coated, which is too few to support a dimension. Revisit only with measured ASTM C1371 values and an expanded metals set.
dropped_dimensions.reflectance (solar): Conflated albedo with specular gloss. Split: gloss becomes a scored dimension, solar reflectance becomes L2 data.

scoring.secondary: raw ordinal score, reported alongside kappa for interpretability
scoring.rationale: Any constant answer scores kappa=0 by construction, which closes the trivial-answer exploit while preserving ordinal partial credit.
scoring.confidence_weight: REMOVED. It could only penalise correct low-confidence answers and made scores non-comparable across models.
scoring.required_reporting: Every dimension must be reported with its trivial baseline.

open_work.open_porosity: 107 cells, EN 1936 / EN ISO 10545-3 / ASTM C642
open_work.blocked_on_decision: image-ablation control determines whether vhc and vapour remain scored dimensions; vernacular-material inclusion is a Nour call

provenance_tiers.industry: industry specification or trade body (MPI, Qualicoat, AAMA, CPAA, EN 10088-2 finish tables)
provenance_tiers.database: handbook or material database (ASHRAE HOF, WUFI/IBP, CIBSE, EnergyPlus, LBNL, EPD)
provenance_tiers.estimate: no traceable source; assigned by category analogy
provenance_tiers._ordering: standard > industry > database > literature > manufacturer > trade > estimate

known_limitations: Populated numbers are unit conversions of v2.5 values. No value was independently re-verified against a purchased standard.
gloss_class, vapour_class and open_porosity are null pending 328 researched cells.
The 4-level vhc binning is benchmark convention, not standardised.
Whether vhc and vapour remain SCORED dimensions is unresolved pending the image-ablation control.

14 of 35 scoreable mpcat40 classes are uniform on vhc_class even after 4-level rebinning, so vhc is a free point in those classes. Fixed by lookup v2 (IFC-derived valid sets), not by the hierarchy. Until then those classes must be marked unscored for vhc.
cork uses an ASHRAE linoleum/cork-tile proxy (no cork-tile entry exists); flagged in vhc_proxy_note, not an error.

integrity.method: sha256 of json.dumps({"header":H,"materials":M}, indent=2, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False) with header.self_sha256 and header.integrity removed. sort_keys is required: without it, key insertion order changes the digest.
integrity.verify: python -c "import json,hashlib;D=json.load(open(F));h={k:v for k,v in D['header'].items() if k not in ('self_sha256','integrity')};print(hashlib.sha256(json.dumps({'header':h,'materials':D['materials']},indent=2,ensure_ascii=False).encode()).hexdigest())"

READ_THIS_FIRST.why_so_many_nulls: About 35% of fields are null. That is deliberate. v2.6 is a STRUCTURAL migration: it fixes how the ground truth is organised without inventing any new values. Fields awaiting researched data are null with a needs_source flag so the validator blocks on them, rather than being filled with plausible-looking guesses.

null_and_why.gloss_class, gloss_value, gloss_unit, gl: awaiting per-family measurement, ISO 2813 / EN ISO 10545-18 / ASTM E430 / ISO 7668 (Nour)

substrate_finish_toggles.rationale: Defaults chosen for residential interior prevalence rather than for the most common specification in general practice. Each toggled entry carries a substrate_finish_alternate field.
substrate_finish_toggles.stainless_steel: No.4 brushed, not 2B mill or No.8 mirror

header.substrate_finish_contested_policy: substrate_finish_contested marks entries whose own GU range spans more than one band, whose measurement geometry differs, or whose as-manufactured state differs from the in-service state a photograph would show. Report these separately from the headline figure. Count: see below.
header.one_classification_rule: Exactly one classification field per scored quantity. Superseded schemes live in the changelog, never alongside the active one. This file previously carried both effective_thermal_mass_class and thermal_mass (removed in v2.6) and briefly carried both vhc_class and vhc_class_v3 (removed here).

aac_block_chinese.vhc_source: ISO 10456:2007 Table 3 'Aerated concrete' (rho 400-600, cp=1000). Density grade B05 per GB/T 11968-2006 'Autoclaved aerated concrete blocks' (rho=500 nominal). Jerman et al. 2013 Energy & Buildings 58:36 DOI:10.1016/j.enbuild.2012.11.036 (rho=500,cp~1000,lambda=0.12 for B05). rho=500,cp=1000 -> 500.

level2_areal.note: CRITICAL BOUNDARY: rho*cp = 500 exactly at low/medium threshold. Classification LOW consistent with engineering practice. B03 grade: 300 kJ/m3K (clearly LOW); B07-B08: 700-800 kJ/m3K (MEDIUM).

aac_block_chinese.porosity_notes: Open porosity 65-80% per Jerman et al. 2013 MIP; ASTM C1585-20 sorptivity; EN 772-4 apparent-density methods.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 (fresh cream/white cementitious SR 0.60-0.75); CRRC cementitious masonry category.

aac_block_chinese.visual_descriptors: Very light cream to off-white uniform color when fresh; visibly aerated with small voids (0.5-2mm pores) on saw-cut surface; sharp machine-precise rectangular edges (600x200x100-300mm); lightweight appearance; commonly laid with thin-bed mortar (~3mm joints).
aac_block_chinese.region_notes: Overwhelmingly dominant Chinese infill-wall construction since ~1995; also major in Germany (Ytong/Hebel), Eastern Europe, Middle East.
aac_block_chinese.vlm_scoring_notes: HIGHEST MISCLASSIFICATION RISK. VLM must not default to dense-concrete thermal mass on blocky masonry appearance — AAC is 3-5x lower thermal mass. Key visual cues: visible cellular pores, sharp ground faces, pale cream color, thin-bed joint pattern.
aac_block_chinese.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

acoustic_ceiling_tile.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Acoustical tile' rho=336-368 (use 352),cp=586-795 (use 691)
acoustic_ceiling_tile.porosity_notes: Mineral-fiber or fiberglass core; >0.80 open porosity (Armstrong/USG acoustical datasheets; NRC 0.55-0.90 requires high porosity).

solar_reflectance.source: Armstrong commercial ceilings light-reflectance catalog (white ACT LR 0.80-0.86); IES Lighting Handbook.

acoustic_ceiling_tile.visual_descriptors: Regular 600x600mm or 600x1200mm drop-in panels in exposed T-bar grid; fine fissured or pinhole-perforated white face; slight bow at panel centers.

adobe.vhc_source: Parra-Saldivar & Batty 2006 Building and Environment 41(12):1892 DOI:10.1016/j.buildenv.2005.07.021 (rho~1700, cp 880-1200). Meza et al. 2021 JPCS 1841:012011 DOI:10.1088/1742-6596/1841/1/012011 (rho=1570,cp=1209 -> 1898). Representative rho=1700,cp=1000 -> 1700.
adobe.porosity_notes: Open porosity 28-38% per Meza et al. 2021; NMAC 14.7.4 water-absorption limits; RILEM CPC 11.3.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1; EPA Cool Pavements Compendium 2012 S3 (natural earth surfaces 0.15-0.40).

adobe.visual_descriptors: Discrete rectangular blocks (250-400mm long) with earth mortar joints 15-25mm wide; straw fibre inclusions visible; warm tan to reddish-brown; matte rough surface.
adobe.region_notes: New Mexico (tan-buff SR~0.30), Andes (reddish SR~0.22), Sahel (dark SR~0.18), North Africa (light ochre SR~0.32).
adobe.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

aluminum.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 33 Table 3 aluminum alloy rho=2702,cp=896

level2_areal.note: Window extrusions and cladding sheets 1-3mm -> areal mass 2.4-7.3 kJ/m2K — negligible. ACM/ACP 4mm total -> assembly areal mass <8 kJ/m2K.

aluminum.porosity_notes: Extruded 6xxx alloy; natural oxide (Al2O3) 2-10nm film dense and non-porous per ISO 7599.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 — bare aluminum SR 0.60-0.65; anodized clear similar.

aluminum.visual_descriptors: Silvery metallic surface with brushed, anodized, or mill finish; crisp extruded edges with consistent profile; seen as window frames, railings, ACP cladding with 3-5mm reveal joints.
aluminum.substrate_finish_source: Architectural anodised (Class I) matte-to-satin. Bright-dip would be off-scale.

aluminum_composite_panel.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 33 (aluminum rho=2740,cp=880 -> 2411). ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Polyethylene' (rho=920,cp=2200 -> 2024). Composite 4mm panel = 0.3mm Al + 3.4mm PE + 0.3mm Al -> volume-weighted ~2200 kJ/m3K. Classified LOW because 4mm panel has per-area mass 8.8 kJ/m2K — negligible.

level2_areal.note: CRITICAL: per-volume rho*cp is HIGH but 4mm panel produces NEGLIGIBLE dynamic thermal mass. Classification LOW reflects building-physics effect.

aluminum_composite_panel.porosity_notes: Aluminum skin fully dense (ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 33); PE core non-cellular extruded polymer (<0.5%). ASTM E84 and EN 13501-1.

solar_reflectance.source: CRRC Rated Products Directory metal-wall panel listings (white PVDF SR 0.70-0.82, silver metallic 0.55-0.65, bronze 0.25-0.35, dark anodized 0.08-0.15); Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1.

aluminum_composite_panel.visual_descriptors: Flat perfectly planar rectangular panels (standard 1500x4000mm); uniform metallic PVDF finish; sharp extruded/routed edges; joints typically 10-20mm reveals or silicone-sealed butt joints; high specular highlights on silver/metallic finishes.
aluminum_composite_panel.vlm_scoring_notes: SR is strongly color-dependent. Flammable PE-core products cannot be visually distinguished from mineral-filled core.
aluminum_composite_panel.substrate_finish_note: This entry describes a coating or an integral factory finish, not a bare substrate. Out of scope for a substrate-keyed dimension.

asphalt_bitumen.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Asphalt (bitumen with inert fill)' rho=1602,cp~1050 (Neville — pavement handbooks)
asphalt_bitumen.porosity_notes: Dense-graded HMA 3-8% air voids per Superpave/ASTM D6925; porous asphalt 18-22% (regional variant).

solar_reflectance.source: EPA Cool Pavements Compendium 2012 S1.2 — new asphalt SR 0.05; 5+ years aged SR 0.10-0.20.

asphalt_bitumen.visual_descriptors: Uniformly dark matte-black when new; fading to charcoal-gray as bitumen oxidizes and aggregate is exposed; striped lane paint; joint and crack sealants; tire-polish stripes.
asphalt_bitumen.vlm_scoring_notes: Aged asphalt SR > new asphalt — opposite of most materials; do not apply generic weathering rule.

bamboo_finish.vhc_source: Shah et al. 2016 J. Mater. Sci. 51(6):2991 DOI:10.1007/s10853-015-9610-z (laminated bamboo rho 700-1100, Moso cp 1.80 kJ/kgK). rho=900,cp=1700 -> 1530.

level2_areal.note: Applied as 10-20mm flooring or 8-14mm panel veneer — thin-section limits dynamic storage.

bamboo_finish.porosity_notes: Compressed laminate reduces cell-wall porosity to 4-8% per Shah et al. 2016; resin binder fills interstitial voids.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 (light-tan wood-finish); carbonised bamboo shifts darker to SR~0.25.

bamboo_finish.visual_descriptors: Regular linear glue-laminated strip pattern; warm caramel-tan to light blonde; semi-glossy factory lacquer; nodes subtly visible as thin darker horizontal marks.
bamboo_finish.substrate_finish_note: This entry describes a coating or an integral factory finish, not a bare substrate. Out of scope for a substrate-keyed dimension.

level2_areal.note: Hollow culm geometry (wall thickness 8-18mm) reduces effective per-member thermal mass ~70-85% vs solid cross-section.

bamboo_structural.porosity_notes: Cell-wall open porosity 8-12% (excluding hollow lumen) per ISO 22157:2019 S6; Shah et al. 2016 MIP.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 (natural wood/bamboo SR 0.35-0.45).

bamboo_structural.visual_descriptors: Characteristic hollow cylindrical culms 80-200mm diameter with regular nodes spaced 200-400mm; golden-tan to olive color when new, weathering to silver-gray; glossy waxy cuticle when fresh.
bamboo_structural.substrate_finish_source: Sawn or planed timber, unfinished. Category range for raw substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

brick_clay_facing.vhc_source: EnergyPlus 'M01 100mm brick' rho=1920,cp=790; ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Brick, fired clay, 120 lb/ft3'
brick_clay_facing.porosity_notes: WUFI IBP 'old building brick' 0.24-0.31 m3/m3; ASTM C216 water absorption 4.5-12% by mass (Grade SW/MW) -> >=15% open porosity.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 — red clay brick SR 0.25-0.35.

brick_clay_facing.visual_descriptors: Rectangular modular units ~215x102x65mm in running/Flemish bond with raked or struck mortar joints; faces range from smooth wire-cut to rough sand-faced with variegated red/orange/buff tones and firing flashes.
brick_clay_facing.region_notes: UK engineering brick (BS EN 771-1 Class A) rho=2100-2200, porosity <7% -> semi-porous. South Asian handmade brick rho=1600-1800, porosity 20-28% -> lower thermal mass (~1340 kJ/m3K) and clearly POROUS.
brick_clay_facing.vlm_scoring_notes: Irregular mortar joints and hand-molding texture (frog, warping) indicate South Asian handmade variant.
brick_clay_facing.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

brick_exterior_masonry.vhc_source: EnergyPlus 'Brick - fired clay - 2080 kg/m3 - 102mm' rho=2080,cp=810; ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Brick, fired clay, 130 lb/ft3'
brick_exterior_masonry.porosity_notes: Denser load-bearing extruded brick: WUFI IBP 'solid brick' 0.12-0.18 m3/m3; ASTM C62 Grade SW water absorption <=17% (~10-14% porosity).

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 — red/brown load-bearing clay brick SR 0.22-0.32.

brick_exterior_masonry.visual_descriptors: Thicker units or multi-wythe bonding (English/Flemish) with deep shadow lines at joints; uniform dark-red to chocolate tones; occasional header courses and corbelled details in historic masonry.
brick_exterior_masonry.region_notes: Mediterranean/Iberian hollow clay block (ladrillo hueco) rho~1000, porosity >=30% -> thermal mass MEDIUM (~810) and POROUS. Cavity ends visible on rake course indicate hollow-block regional variant.
brick_exterior_masonry.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

brick_sand_lime_calcium_silicate.vhc_source: ISO 10456:2007 Table 3 'Calcium silicate brick' (rho 1600-2200, cp=1000 ISO default or cp=900 per spec). EN 771-2:2011+A1:2015 density class 1.8 typical. rho=1800,cp=900 -> 1620.
brick_sand_lime_calcium_silicate.porosity_notes: Water absorption <=14% by mass per EN 771-2:2011+A1:2015 (category W2 units 8-12%); volumetric ~15-22% at the semi-porous/porous boundary. BS EN 772-11:2011 capillary test. Classified non-porous per dense high-density class (rho=2000+) convention.
brick_sand_lime_calcium_silicate.porosity_criterion_override: Water absorption <=14% by mass per EN 771-2:2011+A1:2015 (category W2 units 8-12%); volumetric ~15-22% at the semi-porous/porous boundary. BS EN 772-11:2011 capillary test. Classified non-porous per dense high-density class (rho=2000+) convention.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 (white/cream cementitious masonry SR 0.55-0.68 fresh).

brick_sand_lime_calcium_silicate.visual_descriptors: Very pure white to light cream; machine-precise dimensions with sharp square edges (240x115x71mm NF format); dense heavy appearance; fine smooth surface; laid with thin-bed mortar (~2mm) joints in modern construction.
brick_sand_lime_calcium_silicate.region_notes: Dominant in Germany, Netherlands, Belgium, Denmark, parts of Switzerland and Austria.
brick_sand_lime_calcium_silicate.vlm_scoring_notes: SR 0.60 exactly at semi-gloss/gloss threshold — accept either. Key diagnostic vs AAC: no visible aeration pores, higher apparent density, crisper edges.
brick_sand_lime_calcium_silicate.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

carpet.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Pile carpet with rubber pad, 3/8-1/2 in.' rho=288,cp~1380 (NIST 2000)

level2_areal.note: Carpet is thermally insulating — ISOLATES underlying concrete/subfloor from room air; do not assign carpeted slab the bulk concrete mass for interior-air coupling calculations.

carpet.porosity_notes: WUFI tufted fabric data — 0.80-0.95 void fraction; fibrous structure holds substantial air.

solar_reflectance.source: IES Lighting Handbook (10th ed.) — medium-gray commercial carpet luminous reflectance ~0.20 used as SR proxy.

carpet.visual_descriptors: Soft pile surface with visible loop or cut-pile texture; seam and edge tack-strip concealed at perimeter; patterned broadloom or modular tile (500x500mm); often heavily soiled in traffic lanes.
carpet.substrate_finish_note: Fibrous, loose or non-planar surface. Does not present a specular gloss class under ISO 2813.

ceramic_tile_glazed.vhc_source: Garcia et al. 2011 J. Euro Ceramic Soc 31:1359 rho=2000,cp=840. NOT listed in ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1.

level2_areal.note: 8-10mm tile delivers ~16 kJ/m2K; secondary to concrete/mortar substrate which dominates.

ceramic_tile_glazed.porosity_notes: Face vitrified glass coat <0.5%; bisque body 3-10% per ANSI A137.1/ASTM C373 Class BIIa/BIIb. Composite class is semi-porous.

solar_reflectance.source: LBNL Cool Colors Project database — white glazed ceramic SR 0.75-0.80.

ceramic_tile_glazed.visual_descriptors: Uniform dimensional tiles with high specular glaze; sharp square or rectified edges; narrow grout joints (1.5-3mm); reflective highlights; printed or solid-color glaze patterns.
ceramic_tile_glazed.vlm_scoring_notes: Colored and patterned glazed tiles vary across full SR range; default 0.75 applies only to white/light glazes.

substrate_finish_alternate.note: Alternate as-manufactured state. Switch here if the project context differs.

ceramic_tile_glazed.substrate_finish_source: TOGGLED: matte glaze taken as default, being standard in contemporary tile. True matte glazes measure 9-14 GU (Ceramica 69(391), 2023), which sits right on the 10 GU band edge.
ceramic_tile_glazed.substrate_finish_contested_note: Range 9-14 GU straddles the 10 GU matte/semi-gloss edge. Already toggled.

ceramic_tile_porcelain.vhc_source: EPD International S-P-06762 rho=2380-2450 (use 2400); cp=840 from Garcia et al. 2011 J. Euro Ceramic Soc 31:1359
ceramic_tile_porcelain.porosity_notes: ANSI A137.1:2022/ASTM C373-18 classify porcelain as <=0.5% water absorption — vitrified throughout body.

solar_reflectance.source: Daltile Xteriors SRI technical bulletin; cool-roof porcelain paver SR ~0.55.

ceramic_tile_porcelain.visual_descriptors: Large-format rectified tiles (600x600 to 1200x3000mm); through-body coloration; matte or polished finish; often stone or concrete look with digital inkjet patterning; razor-thin grout joints.
ceramic_tile_porcelain.substrate_finish_source: Technical porcelain; wide range by finish.
ceramic_tile_porcelain.substrate_finish_contested_note: Range spans matte (unglazed) to gloss (polished). The finish, not the material, decides.

substrate_finish_alternate.note: Alternate as-manufactured state. Switch here if the project context differs.

ceramic_tile_unglazed.vhc_source: Garcia et al. 2011 J. Euro Ceramic Soc 31:1359 rho=2000,cp=840; cp proxied from fired-clay brick per ASHRAE HOF 2021.
ceramic_tile_unglazed.porosity_notes: ANSI A137.1 Class BIIb/BIII unglazed quarry/terracotta tile water absorption 3-7% by mass -> ~6-12% porosity.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 — red clay tile SR 0.33.

ceramic_tile_unglazed.visual_descriptors: Terracotta or buff-colored matte tiles; slightly irregular edges; exposed aggregate texture; wider grout joints than glazed products; characteristic iron-oxide red tone.

charred_wood_shou_sugi_ban.vhc_source: Friquin 2010 European J. Wood and Wood Products 68(1):109 DOI:10.1007/s00107-009-0380-x (char layer rho=200-400, lambda_char~0.1). BRANZ SR 395 New Zealand (cp_char~1000). rho=300,cp=1000 -> 300 (char layer). Substrate Cryptomeria japonica rho~380-400,cp=1630 per ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Softwoods'. Sandberg & Johansson 2013 Wood Mater. Sci. Eng. 8(1):12 DOI:10.1080/17480272.2012.731935.

level2_areal.note: COMPOSITE: 2-10mm char layer (LOW, 300) over 15-25mm substrate softwood (MEDIUM, ~620). Area-averaged 18mm board ~530 kJ/m3K at LOW/MEDIUM boundary.

charred_wood_shou_sugi_ban.porosity_notes: Char layer forms semi-closed carbon skin; Friquin 2010 char density 200-400 -> char-layer porosity 70-85% but dominated by closed micropores. Substrate remains porous softwood (60-70%). Surface absorption on wire-brushed yakisugi: 5-10% by mass per Sandberg & Johansson 2013.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 (near-black carbon surface SR 0.04-0.12). Wire-brushed/oiled yakisugi slightly higher (0.08-0.12).

charred_wood_shou_sugi_ban.visual_descriptors: Deep near-black surface with visible longitudinal wood-grain texture through char as fine ridged striations; matte to slightly satin (oiled variants); char layer may show fine cracquelure or 'alligator' pattern; installed typically as vertical or horizontal shiplap cladding.
charred_wood_shou_sugi_ban.region_notes: Originated Japan (yakisugi on Cryptomeria japonica / Sugi), now globally applied to pine, larch, oak, accoya.
charred_wood_shou_sugi_ban.vlm_scoring_notes: CRITICAL: despite subtle sheen (especially oiled) integrated SR is 0.05-0.10 — unambiguously MATTE. Do not upgrade to semi-gloss based on specular highlights. Black absorber is matte.
charred_wood_shou_sugi_ban.substrate_finish_source: Raw sumi char as-manufactured. Oiled variant is semi-gloss 10-30 GU.

chinese_glazed_roof_tile.vhc_source: Garcia et al. 2011 J. European Ceramic Society 31(8):1359 DOI:10.1016/j.jeurceramsoc.2011.01.018 (ceramic rho=2000,cp=840). GB/T 21149-2017 'Glazed roof tiles' China (rho 1900-2100). rho=2000,cp=840 -> 1680.
chinese_glazed_roof_tile.porosity_notes: Fired ceramic body 6-12% water absorption per GB/T 21149-2017; surface glaze <0.5% (ISO 10545-3:2018).

solar_reflectance.source: Levinson et al. 2010 Energy & Buildings 42(9):1615 DOI:10.1016/j.enbuild.2010.05.004 cool colored glazed tile surveys; CRRC Rated Products Directory glazed clay tile (aged 0.35-0.62); Berdahl & Bretz 1997.

chinese_glazed_roof_tile.visual_descriptors: High-specular vitrified glaze with strong directional highlight; imperial yellow for palace buildings, emerald green for princely residences, cobalt blue for heaven temples; semi-circular barrel profile with alternating pan and cover rows; elaborate ridge-end caps.
chinese_glazed_roof_tile.region_notes: Imperial yellow SR~0.60 (semi-gloss upper/gloss boundary), emerald green SR~0.35, cobalt blue SR~0.25.
chinese_glazed_roof_tile.vlm_scoring_notes: Multi-color class — accept ANY of matte/semi-gloss/gloss if predicted hue matches observed glaze color.
chinese_glazed_roof_tile.mpcat40_note: NYU40 lacks 'roof' class; ceiling (22) for interior underside, otherstructure (38) for exterior.
chinese_glazed_roof_tile.substrate_finish_source: Traditional glossy glaze. Zellige is hand-glazed and varies point to point.
chinese_glazed_roof_tile.substrate_finish_contested_note: Range 40-90 GU straddles the 70 GU semi-gloss/gloss edge.

chinese_gray_brick_qingzhuan.vhc_source: Wang et al. 2017 Construction and Building Materials 149:638 DOI:10.1016/j.conbuildmat.2017.05.043 (qingzhuan rho=1700,cp=900). Cross-checked vs ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Brick, fired clay' cp=800 (alternative: 1360 kJ/m3K, still HIGH).

level2_areal.note: Value (1530) sits only 2% above HIGH threshold; SR (0.35) sits only 5pp above matte/semi-gloss threshold.

chinese_gray_brick_qingzhuan.porosity_notes: Water absorption 8-15% by mass per GB 5101-2017 'Fired common bricks' -> volumetric open porosity >15%. Hall & Hamilton 2015 Materials and Structures 48(8):2503 DOI:10.1617/s11527-014-0332-5.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 (medium-gray mineral surface SR 0.30-0.40).

chinese_gray_brick_qingzhuan.visual_descriptors: Uniform blue-gray to slate-gray color (never red or orange); matte mineral surface; sharply squared edges; narrow 5-10mm lime-mortar joints; often laid in running or stretcher bond in hutong wall construction.
chinese_gray_brick_qingzhuan.region_notes: Distinctive East Asian material — VLMs trained on Western datasets frequently misclassify as weathered concrete, bluestone, or soot-stained red brick.
chinese_gray_brick_qingzhuan.vlm_scoring_notes: Accept matte for weathered or soot-stained specimens. SR at matte/semi-gloss boundary.
chinese_gray_brick_qingzhuan.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

clay_brick_tropical.vhc_source: Hall & Hamilton 2015 Materials and Structures 48(8):2503 DOI:10.1617/s11527-014-0332-5 (low-fired tropical brick rho 1500-1800, lambda 0.42-0.62; midpoint rho 1650). ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Brick, fired clay' cp=800. rho=1650,cp=800 -> 1320.
clay_brick_tropical.porosity_notes: IS 1077:2017 Class 2 water absorption <=20% by mass; RILEM CPC 11.3; measured 15-25% by mass -> ~28-40% vol porosity.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 (red clay brick SR 0.30-0.40).

clay_brick_tropical.visual_descriptors: Warm orange-red to terracotta, irregular hand-struck or wire-cut faces, visible firing variation; frequently laid with thick (15-20mm) lime-sand mortar joints.
clay_brick_tropical.region_notes: India/SE Asia/Sub-Saharan Africa. Western-trained VLMs will over-estimate density.
clay_brick_tropical.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

clay_roof_tile.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Brick, fired clay, 120 lb/ft3' rho=1920,cp=800 used as analog for fired-clay roof tile. NOTE: EnergyPlus 'F14 Slate or tile' cp=1260 overstates solid-ceramic cp (reflects mortared assembly).
clay_roof_tile.porosity_notes: ASTM C1167 Grade 1/2/3 water absorption 6-20% by mass — porous class.

solar_reflectance.source: CRRC Rated Products Directory — red clay tile Color Family initial SR 0.33.

clay_roof_tile.visual_descriptors: Interlocking S-profile (Mission/Spanish), flat (French), or pantile shapes; warm terracotta color with firing flashes; overlapping courses with visible shadow lines; moss colonization on shaded faces.
clay_roof_tile.region_notes: Japanese kawara (dark smoked/silvered) SR ~0.18 — MATTE. Chinese glazed imperial tiles SR 0.35-0.60 color-dependent (yellow ~0.55, green ~0.40). Indian Mangalore iron-rich deep-red SR 0.20-0.28.

cob.vhc_source: Goodhew & Griffiths 2005 Energy and Buildings 37(5):451 DOI:10.1016/j.enbuild.2004.08.005 (Devon cob cp~1000 J/kgK, lambda 0.6-0.9, rho~1500). Hall & Allinson 2010 CBM 24(12):2484.
cob.porosity_notes: Open porosity 30-42% per Goodhew & Griffiths 2005 and Hall & Allinson 2010; RIML CPC 11.3 applicable.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1. Lime-washed cob shifts to SR~0.60.

cob.visual_descriptors: Monolithic wall with gently undulating irregular curved surface; visible straw fibre; rounded corners; warm earth-brown to golden-tan; frequent lime-wash overcoat; thick walls 500-700mm evident at openings.
cob.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

compressed_earth_block.vhc_source: Ben Mansour et al. 2016 CBM 104:44 DOI:10.1016/j.conbuildmat.2015.12.024 (rho 1610-2194, lambda 0.62-1.48). Turco et al. 2024 CBM (avg dry rho~1800, porosity 24.3%). rho=1800,cp=900 -> 1620. XP P13-901; IS 1725.
compressed_earth_block.porosity_notes: Mean open porosity 24.3% per Turco et al. 2024 meta-analysis; XP P13-901 S5.3; IS 1725:2013 water absorption <=15% by mass.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1; EPA Cool Pavements Compendium 2012 S3 stabilised earth 0.25-0.38.

compressed_earth_block.visual_descriptors: Highly regular rectangular blocks (290x140x90mm typical Auroville module), sharp machine-pressed edges, uniform color, thin cement or earth mortar joints 8-15mm.
compressed_earth_block.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

concrete_cast_in_place.vhc_source: EnergyPlus ASHRAE_2005_HOF_Materials.idf 'M15 200mm heavyweight concrete' rho=2240,cp=900; ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Sand and gravel or stone aggregate concretes, 140 lb/ft3'

level2_areal.note: Typical 100-200mm slab yields 200-400 kJ/m2K effective areal mass.

concrete_cast_in_place.porosity_notes: WUFI IBP 'Concrete C35/45' open porosity ~0.18 m3/m3; Lstiburek BSI-002 capillary-active concrete.

solar_reflectance.source: Levinson & Akbari 2001 LBNL-48334 — new ordinary Portland SR 0.35-0.40; weathered gray SR 0.25.

concrete_cast_in_place.visual_descriptors: Uniform mid-gray matte surface with form-tie holes, faint horizontal cold-joint lines, occasional air-pocket bugholes, slightly mottled cementitious texture; fine aggregate may be visible where surface is ground.
concrete_cast_in_place.vlm_scoring_notes: Confounded with cement plaster/stucco at close range — form-tie holes and aggregate visibility are distinguishing cues.
concrete_cast_in_place.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

concrete_pavement.vhc_source: EnergyPlus 'M15 200mm heavyweight concrete' rho=2240,cp=900; ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Sand and gravel or stone aggregate concretes, 140 lb/ft3'
concrete_pavement.porosity_notes: Dense-graded pavement 10-15% (WUFI IBP 'Concrete C35/45'); pervious pavement variant 15-35% per ACI 522R -> POROUS band.

solar_reflectance.source: EPA Cool Pavements Compendium 2012 Fig.4 — new conventional gray Portland pavement SR ~0.40; aged SR ~0.25.

concrete_pavement.visual_descriptors: Broom-finish or exposed-aggregate horizontal surface; sawn control joints at regular spacing; tire-track soiling; occasional curing-compound sheen on new pours.
concrete_pavement.region_notes: Pervious/porous concrete (ACI 522R) shifts porosity to POROUS (15-35%) and reduces effective density to ~1800 kg/m3. Visible surface voids (popcorn texture) indicate pervious variant.
concrete_pavement.vlm_scoring_notes: Visible surface voids indicate pervious variant — reclassify porosity to porous.
concrete_pavement.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

concrete_precast.vhc_source: EnergyPlus 'M15 200mm heavyweight concrete' rho=2240,cp=900; ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Sand and gravel or stone aggregate concretes, 140 lb/ft3'
concrete_precast.porosity_notes: Typical precast w/c 0.35-0.45 gives 8-14% open porosity (WUFI IBP 'Concrete C35/45'); denser than CIP.

solar_reflectance.source: Levinson & Akbari 2001 LBNL-48334 (new precast with OPC 0.35-0.45; gray precast 0.35).

concrete_precast.visual_descriptors: Crisper edges and smoother as-cast faces than CIP; visible panel joints with sealant; occasional exposed-aggregate finish; consistent light-gray tone with shuttering witness marks.
concrete_precast.region_notes: In Europe and China 'precast panel' frequently denotes AAC (rho=400-700, cp~1000) -> rho*cp=400-700 kJ/m3K -> LOW thermal mass and porous (>60%). Visual cue: smooth chalky white, tongue-and-groove edges.
concrete_precast.vlm_scoring_notes: If panel appears chalky white and lightweight (no aggregate), classify as AAC variant (LOW mass, porous) rather than dense precast.
concrete_precast.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

concrete_roof_tile.vhc_source: rho~2100,cp=840 derived from ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 concrete entries (not a separate Table 1 row); cross-checked with CEN EN 490 concrete roof tile densities.
concrete_roof_tile.porosity_notes: ASTM C1492/EN 490 water absorption data indicate 6-13% porosity for Portland-cement based roof tiles.

solar_reflectance.source: CRRC Rated Products Directory — concrete roof tile, gray Color Family, SR ~0.25.

concrete_roof_tile.visual_descriptors: Uniform tile shape (flat or low-profile S) with slightly rougher texture than clay; mineral pigment coloration (brick-red, terracotta, charcoal, gray); machined-precise edges and interlocks.
concrete_roof_tile.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

coral_aggregate_concrete.porosity_notes: Open porosity 16-24% per Da et al. 2016 vacuum saturation; coral aragonite/calcite clasts vesicular (skeleton porosity 25-40%). ASTM C642.

solar_reflectance.source: Levinson et al. 2010 LBNL-2007E (weathered light concrete 0.40-0.55); Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1.

coral_aggregate_concrete.visual_descriptors: Pale cream to light gray concrete matrix with distinctive white coral/shell clast inclusions (5-25mm angular particles showing skeletal structure); matte to slightly weathered surface.
coral_aggregate_concrete.region_notes: Maldives, Pacific Islands, South China Sea, Caribbean heritage.
coral_aggregate_concrete.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

cork.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Linoleum/cork tile, 1/4 in.' rho=465 as closest proxy; cp~1900 per ISO 10456; EN 13170 expanded cork board.
cork.porosity_notes: Closed-cell suberin structure with 50-60% void fraction; water absorption EN 12087 <3% but air porosity high.

solar_reflectance.source: Oke Boundary Layer Climates Table 1.1 natural cork ~0.30.

cork.visual_descriptors: Honey-to-tan mottled surface with characteristic speckled cellular pattern; warm matte finish; modular tile or sheet format; visible bound-agglomerate granule edges.
cork.vhc_proxy_note: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 has no cork-tile entry; "Linoleum/cork tile, 1/4 in." used as the closest proxy. This is cork TILE (floor/wall finish, ~465 kg/m3), not cork insulation board (120-240 kg/m3). Flagged as a proxy, not an error.
cork.substrate_finish_source: Sawn or planed timber, unfinished. Category range for raw substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

corrugated_metal_tropical.vhc_source: EnergyPlus Materials.idf 'F08 Metal surface' (rho=7824,cp=500 -> 3912). ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 33 carbon steel cp=500. AS 1397:2011.

level2_areal.note: CRITICAL: 0.4-0.5mm gauge sheet -> areal mass only 3-4 kg/m2 -> effective thermal capacitance <2 kJ/m2K. NEGLIGIBLE at envelope scale.

corrugated_metal_tropical.porosity_notes: ASTM A653/A653M galvanized; AS 1397:2011 Zincalume: continuous metallic coating porosity <0.1%.

solar_reflectance.source: CRRC Rated Products Directory bare galvanized/Zincalume (new SR 0.60-0.67, 3-yr aged SR 0.25-0.40); Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1.

corrugated_metal_tropical.visual_descriptors: Sinusoidal or trapezoidal profile (76-100mm pitch); silvery-white spangled (hot-dip galv), uniform matte-silver (Zincalume), or factory color; rust-streaking, moss overgrowth, patchy replacement panels common in tropical vernacular context.
corrugated_metal_tropical.vlm_scoring_notes: Aged corrugated metal falls to SR 0.25-0.40 = semi-gloss or matte. Profile pitch and rib geometry are most reliable visual identifiers regardless of color/age.
corrugated_metal_tropical.substrate_finish_source: Bright as-manufactured; migrates to matte with patina, spangle-dulling or pre-weathering.

substrate_finish_alternate.note: IN-SERVICE state. A photographed roof is usually weathered rather than as-manufactured, so this alternate is the likelier match for scene data.

corrugated_metal_tropical.substrate_finish_contested_note: As-manufactured is bright, in-service is matte. Scene photographs show the in-service state.

cross_laminated_timber_clt.vhc_source: FPInnovations CLT Handbook Canada 2019 Ch 2 (rho=490,cp=1600,lambda=0.12 for spruce-pine-fir per EN 16351:2015+A1:2017). ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Softwoods — Douglas fir' cp=1630,rho=500 -> 815 (cross-check still MEDIUM). ETA-11/0190 Stora Enso CLT rho=480.
cross_laminated_timber_clt.porosity_notes: Intrinsic wood porosity 60-70% per ISO 10456:2007 'Softwood'; CLT adds <1% glue-line volume. Vapour permeability mu~30-50 per EN ISO 12572:2016.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 (fresh softwood SR 0.35-0.50). Weathered CLT drifts to 0.25-0.30 over 6-24 months.

cross_laminated_timber_clt.visual_descriptors: Large-format panels with visible orthogonal lamella pattern; face lamellae run one direction with cross-lamellae edges visible as striped end-grain; lamella width typically 80-240mm with clear finger-joints; pale honey-blond color when fresh; often exposed architecturally as feature walls, ceilings, soffits.
cross_laminated_timber_clt.vlm_scoring_notes: Visual diagnostic: cross-lamella end-grain visible at panel edges distinguishes CLT from glulam (parallel grain only).
cross_laminated_timber_clt.substrate_finish_source: Sawn or planed timber, unfinished. Category range for raw substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

eifs_stucco.vhc_source: Composite assembly: EPS core (EnergyPlus EPS rho=24,cp=1210 -> 29 kJ/m3K) + 10mm acrylic finish (EnergyPlus 'F07 25mm stucco' rho=1856,cp=840 -> 1559). Area-averaged volumetric for typical 75mm EPS + 10mm render ~80 kJ/m3K.

level2_areal.note: Finish coat 10mm -> areal mass ~15.6 kJ/m2K; total assembly ~18 kJ/m2K — effectively LOW. Surface thermal behavior governed by thin render only.

eifs_stucco.porosity_notes: EPS core closed-cell (non-porous); acrylic polymer-modified render 8-12% porosity; BSC BSD-146 notes assembly water-resistant but not waterproof.

solar_reflectance.source: LBNL Cool Walls project/Heat Island Group — standard light-colored EIFS SR 0.55-0.65.

eifs_stucco.visual_descriptors: Smooth to coarse-sanded finish coat with expansion joints at 1.2-2.4m; aesthetic reveals and control joints; pastel earth-tone colors; hollow tap-sound; typically hung on sheathing with visible base-of-wall flashing.
eifs_stucco.region_notes: North American EIFS (ASTM E2568) is LOW thermal mass assembly. European ETICS cement/lime render over brick/block (EN 998-1) is HIGH thermal mass from structural wall. Visual identification of substrate critical.
eifs_stucco.vlm_scoring_notes: EIFS and traditional cement stucco look identical to VLMs at face — substrate visible at window reveals is the only reliable differentiator.
eifs_stucco.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

engineered_wood.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Plywood (Douglas fir), 5/8 in.' rho=545,cp=1884 (Kumaran 2002); EN 13986 OSB/LVL rho=600-650.
engineered_wood.porosity_notes: Laminated veneers with phenolic adhesive; WUFI IBP 'Plywood' open porosity ~0.55 m3/m3.

solar_reflectance.source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 2 (plywood SR ~0.35).

engineered_wood.visual_descriptors: Visible layered edge (plywood) or oriented flake surface (OSB); veneer face may be sanded smooth with random grain run; stamped grade marks on back.
engineered_wood.substrate_finish_note: This entry describes a coating or an integral factory finish, not a bare substrate. Out of scope for a substrate-keyed dimension.

exposed_aggregate_concrete.vhc_source: Same bulk as cast-in-place: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Concrete, normal weight'. ACI 303R-12.
exposed_aggregate_concrete.porosity_notes: Surface-layer porosity 2-8% per ACI 303R-12 S5; ASTM C642 boiled absorption.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1; Levinson et al. 2010 LBNL-2007E (aggregate-exposed 0.30-0.55). Dark basalt aggregate SR~0.20.

exposed_aggregate_concrete.visual_descriptors: Pebbled/speckled surface texture with visible 5-25mm angular or rounded aggregate; aggregate color determines overall cast; rough tactile surface.
exposed_aggregate_concrete.region_notes: Aggregate color palette shifts with local geology.
exposed_aggregate_concrete.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

fabric_upholstery.vhc_source: No ASHRAE HOF Table 1 entry. Hens 'Building Physics — Heat, Air and Moisture' rho~130,cp~1300 for typical woven polyester/cotton upholstery.
fabric_upholstery.porosity_notes: Woven textiles over foam cushion; >0.80 void fraction typical.

solar_reflectance.source: IES Lighting Handbook fabric reflectance tables — mid-tone upholstery ~0.30 luminous reflectance used as SR proxy.

fabric_upholstery.visual_descriptors: Woven pile or flat weave on sofas, chairs, drapes, pillows; patterned or solid tones; visible fiber texture and piping/seams; may show wear and soiling on arms/seat cushions.
fabric_upholstery.vlm_scoring_notes: Huge color variance; default SR 0.30 applies to neutral/mid tones only.
fabric_upholstery.substrate_finish_note: Fibrous, loose or non-planar surface. Does not present a specular gloss class under ISO 2813.

fiber_cement_board.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 cement plaster row (rho=1860,cp=840) as matrix proxy; ISO 10456:2007 'Fibre cement' (rho 1200-1400, cp=840). rho=1300,cp=840 -> 1092. ASTM C1186.
fiber_cement_board.porosity_notes: Open porosity 8-14% per ASTM C1185 (water absorption 10-12% by mass); BS EN 12467:2012 Annex C.

solar_reflectance.source: CRRC Rated Products Directory fiber-cement listings (factory-painted white SR 0.70-0.80, light colors 0.45-0.60, medium 0.25-0.40, dark 0.06-0.15). Unprimed gray SR~0.30.

fiber_cement_board.visual_descriptors: Flat or woodgrain-embossed planks/panels; matte factory-painted finish; clean straight edges; nail heads visible; uniform color.
fiber_cement_board.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

foam_insulation_exposed.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1: EPS molded beads rho=16-29 (use 24),cp=1465 (Kumaran 1996) -> 35; XPS rho=22-58,cp=1465; Polyiso rho=26-37,cp=1465.
foam_insulation_exposed.porosity_notes: Closed-cell foam morphology. BSC BSI-038 XPS/PU water absorption <2% (ASTM C272/C578) -> non-porous (cells are sealed).

solar_reflectance.source: CRRC/manufacturer datasheets — white EPS SR 0.65; pink XPS (Owens Corning Foamular) SR ~0.35; blue XPS (Dow Styrofoam) SR ~0.25. Representative mid-range 0.45.

foam_insulation_exposed.visual_descriptors: Bead-patterned white EPS; smooth pink or blue XPS boards with tongue-and-groove edges; foil-faced polyiso with silver reflective surface and printed manufacturer logo.

glass_block.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Architectural glass' (rho=2531,cp=879). Assembly with cavity: effective rho~400 on full-block-volume basis; cp=879 -> ~352. Representative 380. EN 1051-1:2018.

level2_areal.note: Full-block volume dominated by enclosed air/vacuum cavity; poor dynamic thermal mass.

glass_block.porosity_notes: Soda-lime glass zero porosity; internal cavity is sealed macroscopic void. EN 1051-1:2018 S5 requires hermetic seal.

solar_reflectance.source: LBNL IGDB records for Pittsburgh Corning and Seves products; EN 410:2011; NFRC 200/300.

glass_block.visual_descriptors: Regular square/rectangular translucent modules (190x190x80mm typical); visible interior light transmission; pressed-pattern surface texture; mortar joints 8-10mm.
glass_block.mpcat40_note: 9 (window) if daylighting element; 1 (wall) if solid partition; 38 otherwise.
glass_block.substrate_finish_source: Moulded glass; slightly below flat float.
glass_block.substrate_finish_contested_note: Range 70-85 GU sits on the 70 GU edge.

glass_clear_float.vhc_source: EnergyPlus 'F09 Opaque spandrel glass' rho=2528,cp=880; ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 'Architectural (soda-lime float) glass' rho=2531,cp=879

level2_areal.note: CRITICAL: 6mm glass areal mass = 2225 x 0.006 = 13.4 kJ/m2K — negligible. Bulk HIGH classification misleads; use effective LOW for assembly-level modeling.

glass_clear_float.porosity_notes: Amorphous vitreous silicate; open porosity effectively 0% (BS EN 572-1).

solar_reflectance.source: LBNL IGDB/NFRC 300 — Guardian Clear 6mm rho_e,front=0.08 at normal incidence.

glass_clear_float.visual_descriptors: Transparent with faint green edge tint; high specular reflectance at oblique angles; silvered or anodized frame joints; visible spacer bar in IGUs.
glass_clear_float.vlm_scoring_notes: Transparency means VLM often sees through to background — classification must use frame/spacer cues and surface specular highlights, not pixel color.
glass_clear_float.mpcat40_note: mpcat40=21 (mirror) is intentional — highly reflective glass surfaces are annotated as 'mirror' in Matterport3D. mpcat40=40 (misc) covers spandrel panels and structural glazing elements.
glass_clear_float.substrate_finish_source: Fire-polished float surface is specular. Tinting colours the body and leaves the surface unchanged.

glass_curtain_wall.vhc_source: EnergyPlus 'F09 Opaque spandrel glass' rho=2528,cp=880; ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 'Architectural (soda-lime float) glass'

level2_areal.note: IGU assembly (6-12-6mm glass) total glass ~30 kJ/m2K; energy-modeling effective class LOW.

glass_curtain_wall.porosity_notes: All glass/PVB constituents non-porous per BS EN 572-1 and ASTM C1172.

solar_reflectance.source: LBNL IGDB typical low-e IGU (Guardian SunGuard, Saint-Gobain SGG) — exterior hemispherical SR 0.15-0.30.

glass_curtain_wall.visual_descriptors: Large modular glazing units in extruded aluminum stick/unitized grid; visible vertical mullions and horizontal transoms; reflective sky pattern; spandrel panels at slab edges.
glass_curtain_wall.substrate_finish_source: Reflective-coated variants exceed the 0-100 coating scale.

glass_frosted.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 'Architectural (soda-lime float) glass' rho=2531,cp=879

level2_areal.note: 6mm areal mass 13.4 kJ/m2K — negligible.

glass_frosted.porosity_notes: Acid-etched or sandblasted microtexture alters surface optics only; bulk non-porous silicate.

solar_reflectance.source: LBNL IGDB/NFRC 300 — surface microtexture diffuses specular; hemispherical SR ~0.10.

glass_frosted.visual_descriptors: Translucent white appearance that blurs objects behind; uniform diffuse glow; fingerprints show distinctly; used in shower doors and partition panels.
glass_frosted.substrate_finish_source: Acid-etched or sandblasted surface; roughening collapses specular gloss.

glass_tempered.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 'Architectural (soda-lime float) glass' rho=2531,cp=879 — tempering is heat-treatment only; substrate unchanged.

level2_areal.note: Tempered panels 6-19mm give areal mass 13-42 kJ/m2K — negligible.

glass_tempered.porosity_notes: Soda-lime silicate; non-porous per BS EN 12150-1.

solar_reflectance.source: NFRC 300/LBNL IGDB — clear tempered indistinguishable spectrally from float at rho_e=0.08.

glass_tempered.visual_descriptors: Chamfered/polished edges; etched safety logo in corner; slight roller-wave distortion visible in reflections; occasional iridescent 'strain pattern' in polarized light.
glass_tempered.substrate_finish_source: Fire-polished float surface is specular. Tinting colours the body and leaves the surface unchanged.

glass_tinted.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 'Architectural (soda-lime float) glass' rho=2531,cp=879 — tint is ppm-level body colorant, unchanged substrate.

level2_areal.note: Same 6mm areal mass 13.4 kJ/m2K — negligible.

glass_tinted.porosity_notes: Identical soda-lime substrate; BS EN 572-1 — non-porous.

solar_reflectance.source: LBNL IGDB tinted float records (gray, bronze, green, blue-green bodies) SR ~0.05 at face.

glass_tinted.visual_descriptors: Visibly darkened (bronze/gray/green/blue) with reduced transmission; from exterior appears mirror-dark against sky; retains specular surface reflections.
glass_tinted.substrate_finish_source: Fire-polished float surface is specular. Tinting colours the body and leaves the surface unchanged.

glulam.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Softwoods — Douglas fir/larch' cp=1630,rho=530 (GL24h/GL28h per EN 14080:2013) -> 864. ANSI/APA PRG 320 confirms density 480-580 for common softwood. ISO 10456:2007 'Softwood' cross-check (800 kJ/m3K — MEDIUM).
glulam.porosity_notes: Same softwood porosity 60-70% per ISO 10456:2007; glue-lines add <0.5% non-porous volume per EN 14080:2013 Annex.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 (oiled/natural softwood SR 0.30-0.45).

glulam.visual_descriptors: Long linear structural members (beams, columns, arches) with clearly visible horizontal lamination lines every 38-45mm; all laminations parallel (contrast to CLT); light honey to medium tan; often clear-finished or lightly oiled.
glulam.vlm_scoring_notes: Key diagnostic vs CLT: all laminations parallel, member is linear (beam/column) not planar (panel).
glulam.mpcat40_note: Structural beam/column — no NYU40 class for beams; otherstructure (38).
glulam.substrate_finish_source: Sawn or planed timber, unfinished. Category range for raw substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

grass_turf.vhc_source: Sailor & Hagos 2011 Energy & Buildings 43:2298 — moist soil substrate rho~1200,cp~1000.
grass_turf.porosity_notes: Rooted mineral soil >=40% total porosity (ASTM D7263); above-ground biomass adds air-filled canopy porosity.

solar_reflectance.source: Oke Boundary Layer Climates Table 1.1 — short green vegetation SR 0.20-0.25.

grass_turf.visual_descriptors: Uniform green blade texture with mow striping; edged at hardscape joints; seasonal color shift to brown in dry/dormant periods; occasional bare patches.
grass_turf.region_notes: C3 cool-season (Kentucky bluegrass, fescue) SR 0.23-0.26. C4 warm-season (Bermuda, zoysia) browner SR 0.18-0.22. Dormant turf SR drops to 0.15.
grass_turf.substrate_finish_note: Fibrous, loose or non-planar surface. Does not present a specular gloss class under ISO 2813.

gravel_crushed_stone.vhc_source: No ASHRAE HOF Table 1 direct row. Bulk gravel rho~1600,cp~900 from Engineering Toolbox cross-checked against ASHRAE limestone/granite cp entries (795-837).
gravel_crushed_stone.porosity_notes: Loose aggregate bed 30-40% inter-particle void fraction per ASTM C29.

solar_reflectance.source: EPA Cool Pavements Compendium 2012 Table 2 — gravel ballast SR 0.20-0.35.

gravel_crushed_stone.visual_descriptors: Loose angular or rounded stones 10-40mm; multicolor (gray/buff/pink) with shadowed interstices; raked or compacted pattern; occasional wheel ruts.
gravel_crushed_stone.region_notes: Limestone gravel SR 0.30-0.40; basalt/trap-rock SR 0.10-0.15 (dark, matte); white marble chip SR 0.60+ (gloss). Regional geology dominates classification.
gravel_crushed_stone.substrate_finish_note: Fibrous, loose or non-planar surface. Does not present a specular gloss class under ISO 2813.

green_roof.vhc_source: Sailor & Hagos 2011 Energy & Buildings 43:2298 + EnergyPlus 'Material:RoofVegetation' substrate default rho=1100,cp=1200 per EnergyPlus Engineering Reference
green_roof.porosity_notes: FLL Dachbegrünungsrichtlinie 2018 total porosity >=45% with 10-20% air-filled at field capacity; ASTM E2399/E2400 test methods.

solar_reflectance.source: EPA Cool Roofs Compendium Ch 2/Sproul et al. 2014 Energy & Buildings 71:20 — extensive green-roof SR ~0.25.

green_roof.visual_descriptors: Continuous vegetated mat (sedum, grasses, herbaceous perennials) with visible growing media at edges; gravel ballast margin; drainage outlets; seasonal flowering and dormancy color changes.
green_roof.region_notes: Extensive sedum roofs in temperate climates SR 0.20-0.25. Intensive roof gardens SR 0.15-0.22. Dried-out summer sedum shifts reddish and SR drops.
green_roof.substrate_finish_note: Fibrous, loose or non-planar surface. Does not present a specular gloss class under ISO 2813.

gypsum_board.vhc_source: EnergyPlus 'G01a 19mm gypsum board' rho=800,cp=1090 -> 872. NOTE disagreement: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 'Gypsum or plaster board' rho=641,cp=879 -> 564 kJ/m3K (Kumaran 2002); source reflects different board densities Type X vs regular.
gypsum_board.porosity_notes: WUFI IBP 'Gypsum Board' open porosity ~0.65 m3/m3; large pore structure from hemihydrate-to-dihydrate rehydration voids.

solar_reflectance.source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 2 — paper-faced gypsum white SR 0.60-0.70.

gypsum_board.visual_descriptors: Smooth paper-faced board with taped-and-finished joints; screw-dimples at 300mm spacing; off-white ivory ground before paint; faint horizontal/vertical seams in raking light.
gypsum_board.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

gypsum_plaster_juss.vhc_source: Binici et al. 2014 CBM 54:204 DOI:10.1016/j.conbuildmat.2013.12.046 (traditional gypsum-earth plasters rho 850-1100 midpoint 975, lambda 0.26-0.52). cp=840 from ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Gypsum plaster, sand aggregate' (primary anchor). IS 2547:2005. rho=975,cp=840 -> 819.
gypsum_plaster_juss.porosity_notes: Binici et al. 2014 open porosity 25-40% for traditional low-calcined juss; RILEM TC 203-RHM recommendations for historic gypsum.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 (cream/off-white plaster SR 0.50-0.60).

gypsum_plaster_juss.visual_descriptors: Cream to off-white matte-to-slightly-satin finish; softer and more irregular than modern skim plaster; visible trowel marks and color mottling; often carved/incised into geometric motifs in Iraqi/Iranian/Najdi interiors.
gypsum_plaster_juss.region_notes: Iraq, Iran, Gulf, Egypt, Levant. Distinct from European gypsum plaster (harder, denser) and from modern drywall.
gypsum_plaster_juss.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

hardwood_maple.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Hardwoods — Maple' rho=641-705 (use 673),cp=1633 (Kumaran 2002)
hardwood_maple.porosity_notes: Diffuse-porous anatomy; WUFI IBP maple ~0.55 m3/m3 void fraction.

solar_reflectance.source: LBNL Cool Walls project dataset — light wood species (maple, birch) SR ~0.45.

hardwood_maple.visual_descriptors: Pale creamy white-to-blonde with subtle fine tight grain; occasional bird's-eye or curly figure; very uniform sapwood-dominant appearance on sports floors and cabinetry.
hardwood_maple.substrate_finish_source: Sawn or planed timber, unfinished. Category range for raw substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

hardwood_oak.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Hardwoods — Oak' rho=657-753 (use 700),cp=1633 (Wilkes 1979 per Kumaran 2002)
hardwood_oak.porosity_notes: WUFI IBP 'Oak (hardwood)' open porosity 0.50-0.55 m3/m3; ring-porous anatomy with large earlywood vessels.

solar_reflectance.source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 2 (medium wood SR 0.30); Oke Boundary Layer Climates Table 1.1.

hardwood_oak.visual_descriptors: Pronounced open-grain with ray flecks visible on quarter-sawn boards; warm honey-to-tawny tones darkening with age; matte to satin clear finish; tongue-and-groove floor joints.
hardwood_oak.substrate_finish_source: Sawn or planed timber, unfinished. Category range for raw substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

hempcrete.vhc_source: Collet & Pretot 2014 CBM 65:600 DOI:10.1016/j.conbuildmat.2014.05.056 (rho 291-336, cp 1250-1557, lambda 0.09-0.11). rho=313,cp=1400 -> 438. ACERMI-certified product datasheets.
hempcrete.porosity_notes: Total porosity 72-78% (intra-shiv + inter-particle) per Collet & Pretot 2014 MIP; WUFI IBP 'Hemp-lime' entry.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 (light tan-cream mineral surface); EPA Cool Pavements Compendium 2012 S4.

hempcrete.visual_descriptors: Cast monolithic appearance with slight aggregate texture from hemp shiv particles; light cream to pale tan color; matte semi-rough surface; non-load-bearing infill around visible timber frame.
hempcrete.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

kawara_tile_japanese.vhc_source: Garcia et al. 2011 J. European Ceramic Society 31(8):1359 DOI:10.1016/j.jeurceramsoc.2011.01.018 (fired-clay ceramic rho~1900,cp=840). JIS A 5208:2014 'Clay roofing tiles' (Type I density class, water absorption <=12%). rho=1900,cp=840 -> 1596.
kawara_tile_japanese.porosity_notes: Water absorption 10-15% per JIS A 5208:2014 Table 3 (ibushi-gawara type typically 11-13%); open porosity >15% by volume.

solar_reflectance.source: Levinson et al. 2010 Energy & Buildings 42(9):1615 DOI:10.1016/j.enbuild.2010.05.004 (dark unglazed clay tile); CRRC Rated Products Directory unglazed clay tile (aged SR 0.15-0.25 for dark gray); Berdahl & Bretz 1997.

kawara_tile_japanese.visual_descriptors: Deep blue-gray to near-black with soft metallic sheen from smoke-firing (carbon deposition); fine ceramic grain visible; J-profile san-kawara most common with interlocking side flanges; steep pitch with visible horizontal course lines.
kawara_tile_japanese.region_notes: Japan, Korean (gi-wa), some traditional Taiwanese contexts.
kawara_tile_japanese.vlm_scoring_notes: Despite subtle specular sheen from carbon reduction layer, integrated SR remains below 0.30 — matte is correct.
kawara_tile_japanese.substrate_finish_source: TOGGLED: ibushi carbon-smoked silvery finish taken as default.

laterite_stone_block.vhc_source: IS 3620:1979 reaffirmed Laterite Stone Block for Masonry (rho 1600-2000 kg/m3). Uma & Rashmin 2024 ENERGISE proceedings (Dakshina Kannada laterite wall, time-lag 7h, implying rho*cp~1500). cp proxy from ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 porous limestone (cp~840). rho=1800,cp=840 -> 1512.
laterite_stone_block.porosity_notes: Open porosity 28-42%; IS 3620:1979 water-absorption test; Kasthurba et al. 2007 CBM 21(1):132 DOI:10.1016/j.conbuildmat.2005.06.046.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 (deep-red mineral surface 0.18-0.28).

laterite_stone_block.visual_descriptors: Regular cut blocks 390x190x190mm; distinctive rust-red to deep-maroon; visible vesicular/pitted surface texture; cement or lime mortar 10-15mm.
laterite_stone_block.region_notes: Konkan/Goa/Kerala/Karnataka India (IS 3620); Coastal West Africa; Sri Lanka.
laterite_stone_block.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

lime_surkhi_plaster.vhc_source: Assael et al. 2010 Int. J. Thermophys. 31:844 DOI:10.1007/s10765-010-0716-x (rho 1700-1850, lambda 0.8-1.0). Cerny et al. 2014 Adv. Mater. Res. 982:1 DOI:10.4028/www.scientific.net/AMR.982.1 (cp~900). rho=1800,cp=900 -> 1620. IS 1344:1981.
lime_surkhi_plaster.porosity_notes: Open porosity 18-28% per Cerny et al. 2014 AMR 982:1; RILEM CPC 11.3.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 (pale-pink mineral plaster 0.45-0.60); EPA Cool Pavements Compendium 2012 S4.

lime_surkhi_plaster.visual_descriptors: Smooth-to-fine-textured render with distinctive pale pink-salmon tint from surkhi; often burnished to slight sheen; applied 15-40mm thick; edges often shaped with mouldings in historic architecture.
lime_surkhi_plaster.region_notes: South Asia: India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Sri Lanka.
lime_surkhi_plaster.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

lime_wash.vhc_source: ISO 10456:2007 Table 3, lime plaster rho=1600 kg/m3, cp=1000 J/kgK, giving 1.600 MJ/m3K bulk. NOTE: an earlier version of this string read 'negligible areal mass; substrate dominates... listed as LOW', which was areal reasoning in a bulk field and contradicted the stored value. v2.6 moved that claim to level2_areal. The bulk value is correct as stored.

level2_areal.note: Coating 0.5-2mm gives negligible areal mass; substrate dominates. This is why v2.5 recorded 0 in the bulk field.

lime_wash.porosity_notes: Santamouris 2012 Advances in Building Energy Research Ch 7; BS EN 459-1:2015 building lime; Ca(OH)2->CaCO3 carbonation leaves 30-50% residual microporosity.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 (fresh white lime SR 0.75); LBNL-48829 Levinson & Akbari 2002; Santamouris 2012 ABER Ch 7 lime-wash SR 0.70-0.85.

lime_wash.visual_descriptors: Chalky white to soft cream; visibly matte texture despite high SR (gloss class is radiometric, not visual); brush-stroked unevenness; slight translucency over textured substrate.
lime_wash.vlm_scoring_notes: IMPORTANT: radiometric SR>0.60 = gloss class, but visual texture is matte. For VLM visual tasks describe as matte white. Aged lime-wash drops to SR 0.50-0.60 within 2-3 years.
lime_wash.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

mdf.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Particleboard, medium density' rho=801,cp=1178 (Lewis 1967) as closest proxy; ANSI A208.2; JIS A 5905:2003.
mdf.porosity_notes: Cellulose fibers bonded with UF/MDI resin; residual pore structure 30-45% by ANSI A208.2 void-fraction data.

solar_reflectance.source: Light-brown engineered wood products SR ~0.40 (industry datasheets, Kronospan/Egger).

mdf.visual_descriptors: Homogeneous tan-brown edge with no visible grain; ultra-smooth machined faces; razor-crisp routed profiles.
mdf.substrate_finish_source: Sawn or planed timber, unfinished. Category range for raw substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

metal_roofing_copper.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 33 Table 3 copper rho=8933,cp=385

level2_areal.note: 0.6mm sheet (16oz/ft2) -> areal mass 2.1 kJ/m2K — negligible.

metal_roofing_copper.porosity_notes: Pure-copper sheet; ASTM B370 material porosity <0.1%.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 — new polished copper SR 0.74; green patina SR 0.35.

metal_roofing_copper.visual_descriptors: Warm orange-pink metallic when new; transitions through brown to matte green patina over 5-25 years; hand-soldered standing seams; batten caps; flashings with clear handcrafted profile.
metal_roofing_copper.vlm_scoring_notes: Aged copper's green patina visually resembles painted green metal — soldered seam pattern is the distinguishing cue.
metal_roofing_copper.substrate_finish_source: Bright mill copper as-manufactured; migrates to matte with patina.

substrate_finish_alternate.note: IN-SERVICE state. A photographed roof is usually weathered rather than as-manufactured, so this alternate is the likelier match for scene data.

metal_roofing_copper.substrate_finish_contested_note: As-manufactured is bright, in-service is matte. Scene photographs show the in-service state.

level2_areal.note: 0.5-1mm cladding -> areal mass 2-4 kJ/m2K — negligible.

metal_roofing_galvanized.porosity_notes: Hot-dip galvanized (ASTM A653) dense zinc coating; ASTM A90 mass tests <0.5% porosity.

solar_reflectance.source: ORNL Kriner 2001 'Metal Roofing Reflectance'/CRRC Rated Products Directory — galvanized steel bare new SR 0.61; weathered SR 0.30.

metal_roofing_galvanized.visual_descriptors: Standing-seam or corrugated profile with characteristic spangled zinc-flower crystallization pattern; bright metallic when new; dulls to flat gray; visible fasteners and clip-locked seams.
metal_roofing_galvanized.substrate_finish_source: Bright as-manufactured; migrates to matte with patina, spangle-dulling or pre-weathering.

substrate_finish_alternate.note: IN-SERVICE state. A photographed roof is usually weathered rather than as-manufactured, so this alternate is the likelier match for scene data.

metal_roofing_galvanized.substrate_finish_contested_note: As-manufactured is bright, in-service is matte. Scene photographs show the in-service state.

metal_roofing_zinc.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 33 Table 3 zinc rho=7140,cp=388

level2_areal.note: 0.7mm sheet areal mass 1.9 kJ/m2K — negligible.

solar_reflectance.source: VMZINC/Rheinzink technical data — pre-weathered zinc SR 0.15-0.25.

metal_roofing_zinc.visual_descriptors: Uniform matte blue-gray to slate-gray factory pre-patina; standing-seam or interlocking shingle profile; crisp folded flashings; subtle variation across panels as surface develops.
metal_roofing_zinc.substrate_finish_source: Bright as-manufactured; migrates to matte with patina, spangle-dulling or pre-weathering.

substrate_finish_alternate.note: IN-SERVICE state. A photographed roof is usually weathered rather than as-manufactured, so this alternate is the likelier match for scene data.

metal_roofing_zinc.substrate_finish_contested_note: As-manufactured is bright, in-service is matte. Scene photographs show the in-service state.

mineral_wool_stone_wool.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Mineral fiber batt/board, glass fiber' (rho 19-64 kg/m3, cp 710-840). EN 13162:2012+A1:2015 stone wool rho=40 (mid-range board grade), cp=840 -> 34. ISO 10456:2007 Table 3 'Mineral wool' cp=1030 -> 41 (both clearly LOW).
mineral_wool_stone_wool.porosity_notes: Open porosity 95-98% per EN 13162:2012+A1:2015 and ISO 10456:2007; air is dominant volumetric phase.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 (light-cream/yellow-gray fibrous mineral SR 0.65-0.75).

mineral_wool_stone_wool.visual_descriptors: Visibly fibrous bulk material with random-oriented stone-wool fibers; light cream to pale yellow-gray; semi-rigid batts or rigid boards; normally concealed — exposed only at construction phase.
mineral_wool_stone_wool.mpcat40_note: Almost always concealed; when visible maps to otherstructure (38).

mirror_reflective_glass.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Architectural glass' (rho=2531,cp=879 -> 2225). Sputter coating ~100nm — negligible mass. NFRC 100/200/300.
mirror_reflective_glass.porosity_notes: Float glass zero open porosity; sputter coating dense PVD film. EN 1279 IGU durability.

solar_reflectance.source: LBNL IGDB reflective-glass records (SR 0.25-0.55 depending on coating); NFRC 300-2020; EN 410:2011.

mirror_reflective_glass.visual_descriptors: Monolithic planar glazing with highly specular mirror-like exterior reflection; tint may be neutral silver, blue-green, bronze, or gold; often in sealed curtain-wall systems.
mirror_reflective_glass.vlm_scoring_notes: Mirror reflection of sky/surroundings is primary VLM cue. SR range 0.25-0.55 overlaps semi-gloss and gloss bands; specific product coating determines exact classification.
mirror_reflective_glass.substrate_finish_source: Silvered; a near-perfect specular reflector. Exceeds the 0-100 coating scale.

mud_plaster_earthen.vhc_source: Hall & Allinson 2010 CBM 24(12):2484 DOI:10.1016/j.conbuildmat.2010.06.002 (earthen plaster rho 1400-1700 midpoint 1550, lambda 0.45-0.80, cp 900-1000 midpoint 950). Jimenez Delgado & Guerrero 2007 CBM 21(5):971 DOI:10.1016/j.conbuildmat.2006.05.021. rho=1550,cp=950 -> 1472.

level2_areal.note: At medium/high boundary (1472 vs 1500 threshold). Applied 10-30mm as finish coat; substrate dominates bulk envelope mass.

mud_plaster_earthen.porosity_notes: Hall & Allinson 2010 direct porosimetry 25-38%; Jimenez Delgado & Guerrero 2007 comparable range; ASTM E2392/E2392M earthen assembly guide.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 (earth-tone mineral finish SR 0.28-0.40); Santamouris 2012 ABER Ch 7.

mud_plaster_earthen.visual_descriptors: Warm earth-tone palette (ochre, sienna, tan); soft rounded surface geometry; visible hand-trowel marks; characteristic fine surface cracking network after drying; integrates with wall as continuous monolithic skin.
mud_plaster_earthen.region_notes: MENA, Sahel (Mali/Burkina Faso Sudano-Sahelian), SW US Pueblo, East Africa.
mud_plaster_earthen.vlm_scoring_notes: SR 0.32 sits immediately above matte threshold (0.30) — dusty specimens drop below 0.30.
mud_plaster_earthen.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

mudbrick_mesopotamian.vhc_source: Dabaieh et al. 2020 J. Cleaner Production 263:121461 DOI:10.1016/j.jclepro.2020.121461 (MENA earthen walls rho 1650-1900 midpoint 1775, lambda 0.45-0.75). Parra-Saldivar & Batty 2006 B&E 41(12):1892 (cp 900-1200 midpoint 1050). rho=1775,cp=1050 -> 1864.

level2_areal.note: Traditional wall thicknesses 400-900mm deliver full diurnal thermal-flywheel performance central to MENA courtyard thermal strategy.

mudbrick_mesopotamian.porosity_notes: Dabaieh et al. 2020 direct measurement 28-38% total porosity; ASTM E2392 earthen assembly guide.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 (light earth-tone); Santamouris 2012 ABER Ch 7 earthen finish SR 0.30-0.45.

mudbrick_mesopotamian.visual_descriptors: Warm ochre-tan to pale khaki; larger format (300x150x75 to 400x200x100mm); thicker (20-35mm) mud-mortar joints; frequent straw-inclusion shadowing; distinctive erosion rounding at parapet edges.
mudbrick_mesopotamian.region_notes: Iraq, Syria, Iran, Gulf. Larger format than New World adobe. Visual prior: brick-size expectation upward.
mudbrick_mesopotamian.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

natural_linoleum.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Linoleum' (rho~1200,cp~1590; Kumaran 2002) -> 1908. ISO 10456:2007; EN ISO 24011:2020; WUFI IBP 'Linoleum' entry (rho 1180-1250,cp 1500-1600). Representative rho=1200,cp=1550 -> 1860.

level2_areal.note: Typical 2.0-4.0mm sheet — per-area mass 2.4-5.0 kg/m2, negligible building-dynamic effect.

natural_linoleum.porosity_notes: Open porosity 3-8% per ISO 24011:2020 S5; WUFI material database 'Linoleum' mu=800-1200.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1; Forbo manufacturer LRV data.

natural_linoleum.visual_descriptors: Smooth uniform flexible sheet/tile with characteristic marbled/mottled pattern throughout thickness (not surface-printed); semi-matte factory sheen; earthy ochres, muted greens, warm grays.
natural_linoleum.vlm_scoring_notes: Through-thickness marbling pattern distinguishes from PVC/vinyl (surface-printed patterns).

paint_matte.vhc_source: Substrate-controlled: EnergyPlus 'G01a 19mm gypsum board' rho=800,cp=1090 (paint film <0.2mm negligible).

level2_areal.note: Paint film itself has negligible thickness; thermal behavior tracks substrate.

paint_matte.porosity_notes: BSC BSI-008 latex film microstructure — 5-15% open porosity in dry paint coat; vapor-permeable by design.

solar_reflectance.source: LBNL Pigment Database — TiO2-pigmented white acrylic latex SR ~0.80.

paint_matte.visual_descriptors: Non-reflective chalky surface with uniform color; subtle roller texture ('orange peel'); no specular hotspots; shows scuffs readily in high-traffic zones.
paint_matte.substrate_finish_note: This entry describes a coating or an integral factory finish, not a bare substrate. Out of scope for a substrate-keyed dimension.

level2_areal.note: Substrate-dominated.

paint_semigloss.porosity_notes: Denser alkyd/acrylic film; 2-5% open porosity per BSC coating-permeability studies — lower than flat/matte due to higher resin loading.

solar_reflectance.source: CRRC Rated Products Directory — white elastomeric/acrylic coating initial SR 0.82 (ENERGY STAR qualifying).

paint_semigloss.visual_descriptors: Reflective sheen visible at grazing angles; smooth film on door/trim/cabinet surfaces; visible brush or roller strokes if not sprayed; specular highlights on casing profiles.
paint_semigloss.substrate_finish_note: This entry describes a coating or an integral factory finish, not a bare substrate. Out of scope for a substrate-keyed dimension.

painted_concrete_exterior.vhc_source: Substrate-controlled: EnergyPlus 'M15 200mm heavyweight concrete' rho=2240,cp=900 (paint film <0.3mm negligible).
painted_concrete_exterior.porosity_notes: Elastomeric/acrylic exterior coating 3-10% porosity (BSC coating permeability data); underlying concrete 10-18% masked by continuous film.

solar_reflectance.source: CRRC Rated Products Directory — white elastomeric/acrylic coatings initial SR 0.80-0.87; ENERGY STAR low-slope coating threshold >=0.65.

painted_concrete_exterior.visual_descriptors: Continuous uniform paint film covering concrete substrate; bridging hairline cracks; visible roller or sprayed texture; control joints still telegraphed through coating.
painted_concrete_exterior.substrate_finish_note: This entry describes a coating or an integral factory finish, not a bare substrate. Out of scope for a substrate-keyed dimension.

painted_metal_exterior.vhc_source: Substrate-controlled: EnergyPlus 'F08 Metal surface' rho=7824,cp=500; factory coating <50um does not alter bulk.

level2_areal.note: 0.5-1.2mm panels -> areal mass 2-4.7 kJ/m2K — negligible.

painted_metal_exterior.porosity_notes: Factory PVDF (Kynar 500/Hylar 5000) or polyester powder coats <2% porosity per AAMA 2605.

solar_reflectance.source: CRRC Rated Products Directory — factory-painted metal panels (Kynar 500/Hylar 5000) span SR 0.30 (dark bronze) to 0.70 (white/cool pigments).

painted_metal_exterior.visual_descriptors: Uniform color with satin-to-semi-gloss sheen; crisp folded/break-formed panel edges; exposed or concealed-fastener profiles; subtle horizontal oil-canning on flat panel expanses.
painted_metal_exterior.vlm_scoring_notes: Color-dependent SR — white cool-roof coatings reach 0.70; dark bronze/charcoal drop to 0.30. Default 0.45 assumes mid-tone.
painted_metal_exterior.substrate_finish_note: This entry describes a coating or an integral factory finish, not a bare substrate. Out of scope for a substrate-keyed dimension.

palm_thatch.vhc_source: Noor et al. 2013 Advanced Materials Research 626:38 DOI:10.4028/www.scientific.net/AMR.626.38 (Nypa fruticans palm frond: lambda 0.05-0.07, rho 80-120 midpoint 100, cp~1300). rho=100,cp=1300 -> 130. CIBSE Guide A 2015 Table 3.12 cross-check.
palm_thatch.porosity_notes: Noor et al. 2013 intrinsic porosity >50% cellular structure; layered assembly adds 30-50% macro-void fraction.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 (dry vegetative surfaces SR 0.15-0.22).

palm_thatch.visual_descriptors: Layered overlapping fronds 600-1500mm long; new installation bright green aging through olive to straw-gold within 6 months then dark gray-brown by year 2-3; fringed bottom edge at eaves; steep pitch >30deg.
palm_thatch.region_notes: Nypa fruticans (SE Asia, Pacific). Distinct from European water-reed: palm fronds wider (20-50mm leaflet-ribs), coarser layered texture, darker tones.
palm_thatch.substrate_finish_note: Fibrous, loose or non-planar surface. Does not present a specular gloss class under ISO 2813.

plaster_cement.vhc_source: EnergyPlus 'F07 25mm stucco' rho=1856,cp=840; ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Cement plaster, sand aggregate' rho=1858,cp=837
plaster_cement.porosity_notes: WUFI IBP 'cement stucco' open porosity 0.24-0.30 m3/m3; denser than lime plaster but still capillary-active.

solar_reflectance.source: Doulos, Santamouris & Livada 2004 Solar Energy 77:231 — gray cement render SR ~0.35; white cement render SR ~0.60.
