plaster_cement.visual_descriptors: Coarse sand-float or dash texture; gray to warm beige; hairline shrinkage cracks; control joints at 3-6m spacing; often paired with masonry substrate.
plaster_cement.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

plaster_lime.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Sand/cement/lime plaster, conditioned' rho=1442,cp~840 (CIBSE Guide A 2006 cross-reference)
plaster_lime.porosity_notes: WUFI IBP 'lime plaster' open porosity ~0.30 m3/m3; high capillary porosity allows vapor transmission — key historic-wall characteristic.

solar_reflectance.source: Santamouris M. (ed.) Advances in Building Energy Research — white lime render SR 0.70-0.85.

plaster_lime.visual_descriptors: Soft matte-white or lime-wash finish with subtle trowel texture; often slightly uneven on historic substrates; occasional pigmented lime-wash pastel tones.
plaster_lime.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

polished_granite_chinese.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Calcitic, dolomitic, limestone, marble, and granite' row (rho=2563,cp=795 -> 2038). ISO 10456:2007 Table 3 'Natural stone — dense crystalline' cross-check.
polished_granite_chinese.porosity_notes: Water absorption 0.1-0.4% per EN 13755:2008 and ASTM C97/C97M-18; non-porous across G603, G654, G562, G664 Chinese varieties.

solar_reflectance.source: Doulos et al. 2004 Solar Energy 77(2):231 DOI:10.1016/j.solener.2004.04.006 (G654 dark Padang SR 0.08-0.15; G603 light Padang SR 0.28-0.45). Berdahl & Bretz 1997.

polished_granite_chinese.visual_descriptors: High-specular mirror-polished surface; visible crystalline grain (2-5mm feldspar and quartz crystals) with dark biotite mica; G654 near-black with silver flecks; G603 medium gray-white 'salt and pepper'; typically 20-30mm thick cladding panels with hairline joints.
polished_granite_chinese.region_notes: G654 dark: matte (0.08-0.15). G603 light: matte/semi-gloss boundary (0.28-0.45). Flamed finish reduces SR 5-10pp.
polished_granite_chinese.vlm_scoring_notes: Polished finish adds strong specular component WITHOUT raising integrated SR — do not upgrade reflectance class based on surface glint.
polished_granite_chinese.substrate_finish_source: Explicitly polished in the material definition.

polished_sealed_concrete_floor.vhc_source: Same substrate as cast-in-place: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Concrete, normal weight' (rho=2240,cp=880 -> 1971).
polished_sealed_concrete_floor.porosity_notes: Lithium silicate densifier + sealer reduces surface open porosity from ~12% to <2% per ASTM C1202 and ASTM C1585. ACI 310R-13.

solar_reflectance.source: Levinson et al. 2011 LBNL Cool Floors report (polished/sealed light-gray concrete SR 0.45-0.55; polished white-cement SR 0.65-0.72); CRRC floor-coatings directory.

polished_sealed_concrete_floor.visual_descriptors: Flat horizontal surface with wet-look semi-gloss sheen; reflections of overhead lighting visible; saw-cut control joints every 3-6m; color uniform gray or pigmented/stained.
polished_sealed_concrete_floor.vlm_scoring_notes: Sheen level is diagnostic — bare concrete slab is matte (SR~0.25); sealed polished is semi-gloss; high-gloss epoxy approaches gloss.
polished_sealed_concrete_floor.substrate_finish_source: CPAA/CPC Level 2 ~20-30, Level 3 ~50-60, Level 4 ~70-80 GU. Varies point to point on aggregated surfaces.
polished_sealed_concrete_floor.substrate_finish_contested_note: Range 20-80 GU spans two bands by grit level. CPAA/CPC L2 is semi-gloss, L4 is gloss.

substrate_finish_alternate.note: Alternate as-manufactured state. Switch here if the project context differs.

rammed_earth.vhc_source: Stefan et al. 2023 Materials 16(17):6015 DOI:10.3390/ma16176015 (rho 1490-2150, cp 701-999 J/kgK; representative rho=1820,cp=850 -> 1547). Hall & Allinson 2010 CBM 24(12):2484 DOI:10.1016/j.conbuildmat.2010.06.002.
rammed_earth.porosity_notes: Open porosity 23-40% per Stefan et al. 2023; IS 2110; Australian HB 195. RILEM CPC 11.3 applicable.

solar_reflectance.source: Levinson & Akbari 2002 LBNL-48829 (red-brown mineral soils SR 0.20-0.35); Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1.

rammed_earth.visual_descriptors: Horizontal striations from layered lift compaction (50-150mm lifts); warm earth tones (ochre, buff, terracotta); matte slightly rough surface; no mortar joints; monolithic wall with possible formwork tie-hole patterns.
rammed_earth.region_notes: Unstabilised dominates MENA, Sahel, Andes, loess China. Cement-stabilised (5-10%) dominates Australia, SW USA, modern European revival.
rammed_earth.vlm_scoring_notes: Distinguishable from adobe by continuous horizontal layering without mortar joints; from CEB by lack of discrete block modules.
rammed_earth.mpcat40_note: Primary wall (1); otherstructure (38) for freestanding elements.
rammed_earth.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

rubber_flooring.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Rubber tile, 1.0 in.' rho=1906,cp~1382

level2_areal.note: CRITICAL: Installed at 3-6mm -> areal mass 7.9-15.8 kJ/m2K — effectively LOW despite high bulk volumetric value. Table-1 row assumes 1.0in thickness never used architecturally.

rubber_flooring.porosity_notes: Vulcanized EPDM/SBR with <2% open porosity per ASTM F1913.

solar_reflectance.source: CRRC Rated Products Directory — dark EPDM roof/floor membranes SR 0.06-0.10.

rubber_flooring.visual_descriptors: Matte black-to-dark-gray surface with studded 'coin-top' or hammered texture; chip-speckled color variants in gyms and healthcare; butt-joint seams.

shoji_screen_washi.vhc_source: Composite area-weighted: washi panel (~0.1mm, negligible) + softwood frame (ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Softwoods' rho=500,cp=1630 -> 815). Area-weighted ~15% frame + 85% paper -> ~450. JIS A 1412-1:1999 thermal resistance test method.

level2_areal.note: Composite assembly: wood frame (~15% area) dominates; paper contribution negligible.

shoji_screen_washi.porosity_notes: Washi highly vapor-permeable; mu<5 per JIS Z 0208:1976 cup method. Wood frame softwood porosity 60-70% per ISO 10456:2007.

solar_reflectance.source: Kamata & Kuwasawa 2014 J. Society of Fiber Science and Technology Japan 70(6):P-141 (washi hemispherical reflectance 0.55-0.65, transmittance 0.30-0.40 for typical kozo washi); Berdahl & Bretz 1997.

shoji_screen_washi.visual_descriptors: Translucent warm-white panels subdivided by fine orthogonal kumiko lattice (30-60mm grid) of softwood mullions; when backlit glows with soft uniform warm-white diffuse light; when lit from viewer side appears near-opaque cream-white with lattice in silhouette; slides in paired tracks.
shoji_screen_washi.region_notes: Almost exclusively Japanese and Japanese-inspired interiors.
shoji_screen_washi.vlm_scoring_notes: SR boundary case at 0.60 exactly at semi-gloss/gloss threshold — accept either. VLM frequently confuses with drywall partition or frosted glass; key diagnostic is visible kumiko lattice.
shoji_screen_washi.substrate_finish_note: Fibrous, loose or non-planar surface. Does not present a specular gloss class under ISO 2813.

softwood_pine.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Softwoods — Southern yellow pine' rho=497,cp=1633 (Kumaran 2002)
softwood_pine.porosity_notes: WUFI IBP 'Southern Pine' open porosity ~0.65 m3/m3; prominent resin canals and earlywood/latewood banding.

solar_reflectance.source: Santamouris wood-surface surveys (Advances in Building Energy Research) — pine unfinished SR ~0.40.

softwood_pine.visual_descriptors: Yellow-to-amber ground with dark latewood stripes and frequent knots; sawn board dimensions standard (2x4, 2x6); often with stamped grade marks.
softwood_pine.substrate_finish_source: Sawn or planed timber, unfinished. Category range for raw substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

softwood_spruce.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Softwoods — Spruce' rho=400,cp=1633 (Kumaran 2002)
softwood_spruce.porosity_notes: WUFI IBP 'Spruce' open porosity ~0.73 m3/m3; fine straight grain with small tracheids.

solar_reflectance.source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 2 (light softwood SR 0.45).

softwood_spruce.visual_descriptors: Very pale cream to pinkish-white with narrow even growth rings; few small tight knots; widely used for SPF framing lumber and CLT laminations.
softwood_spruce.substrate_finish_source: Sawn or planed timber, unfinished. Category range for raw substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

soil_earth.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 S4.6 'Soils' (Salomone & Marlowe 1989) — dry loam rho~1500,cp~900 -> 1350; moist soil at 25% gravimetric water ~2400.
soil_earth.porosity_notes: Natural soils 35-55% total porosity (ASTM D7263); well-compacted fill 25-40%.

solar_reflectance.source: Oke Boundary Layer Climates Table 1.1 — dry bare soil SR ~0.20; wet soil SR ~0.10.

soil_earth.visual_descriptors: Warm brown-to-red-brown mottled surface with crumb or blocky peds; visible cracking when dry; darker and specular when wet; root traces and organic debris.
soil_earth.region_notes: Sandy desert/arid SR 0.35-0.49; dark lateritic/tropical soils SR <0.15; volcanic andosols rho=500-900 shift thermal mass to LOW (~600 kJ/m3K).
soil_earth.vlm_scoring_notes: Soil moisture state controls both color and SR; apparent darkness post-rain does not indicate a different soil type.
soil_earth.substrate_finish_note: Fibrous, loose or non-planar surface. Does not present a specular gloss class under ISO 2813.

stabilised_earth_tile.vhc_source: Morel et al. 2007 Energy & Buildings 39(10):1021 DOI:10.1016/j.enbuild.2006.11.002 (stabilised earth rho 1800-2000 midpoint 1900, cp~860, lambda 0.6-1.1). rho=1900,cp=860 -> 1634. IS 1725:2013; XP P13-901.
stabilised_earth_tile.porosity_notes: IS 1725:2013 water absorption <=15% by mass (stabilised class) -> ~22-30% vol porosity; Morel et al. 2007 direct measurement 20-30% for 5-8% cement stabilisation.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 (light earth-tone masonry SR 0.32-0.45); EPA Cool Pavements/Roofs Compendium 2012 light concrete/earth masonry.

stabilised_earth_tile.visual_descriptors: Uniform red-ochre to buff-tan; clean machine-pressed sharp edges and flat faces; occasional visible fine inclusions or stabilizer segregation.
stabilised_earth_tile.region_notes: India (Auroville Earth Institute), Sub-Saharan Africa (CRATerre), Latin America.
stabilised_earth_tile.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

stainless_steel.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 33 Table 3 '304 stainless steel' rho=7900,cp~500

level2_areal.note: 1.2mm sheet areal mass 4.7 kJ/m2K — negligible.

stainless_steel.porosity_notes: Austenitic 304/316 alloy; passivated Cr2O3 film <5nm; effectively zero porosity (ASTM A480).

solar_reflectance.source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 2 brushed stainless SR 0.50-0.60; LBNL Heat Island Group metallic surfaces dataset.

stainless_steel.visual_descriptors: Cool silver-gray with directional brushed (No.4) or mirror (No.8) finish; fingerprint-prone; seen in handrails, appliances, elevator panels, sinks, kitchen worktops.

substrate_finish_alternate.gu_range: 2B mill or No.8 mirror, off the 0-100 scale
substrate_finish_alternate.note: Alternate as-manufactured state. Switch here if the project context differs.

stainless_steel.substrate_finish_source: TOGGLED: No.4 brushed taken as default, being the common architectural finish on appliances, handrails and panels. Ra 0.4-0.8 um per EN 10088-2 / ASTM A480.

steel_structural.vhc_source: EnergyPlus 'F08 Metal surface' rho=7824,cp=500; ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 33 Table 3 carbon steel rho~7850,cp=500

level2_areal.note: CRITICAL: 6mm plate areal mass 23 kJ/m2K; 1mm cladding 3.9 kJ/m2K — negligible. Only massive thick sections behave as thermal mass.

steel_structural.porosity_notes: Dense metallic crystal with porosity <0.1% (ASTM A36 metallography).

solar_reflectance.source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 2 (painted steel) SR ~0.35; unpainted weathered mill-scale 0.15-0.25.

steel_structural.visual_descriptors: Industrial rolled sections (I-beams, HSS, channels) with bolted or welded connections; factory primer red-brown or intumescent white finish; visible mill marks and rolling stamps.

stone_basalt_volcanic_mena.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Basalt, glass, mica' row (rho=2940,cp=840 -> 2470). Tawayha et al. 2019 Sustainability 11(7):1959 DOI:10.3390/su11071959 (Jordan Hauran basalt lambda 1.3-1.7 confirmed). ISO 10456:2007 dense natural stone cross-check.
stone_basalt_volcanic_mena.porosity_notes: Hauran/Harra dense basalt total porosity <2% by Archimedes (Tawayha et al. 2019). ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 dense basalt bulk; ISO 10456:2007.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 (very dark stone SR 0.05-0.12); Santamouris 2012 ABER Ch 7.

stone_basalt_volcanic_mena.visual_descriptors: Very dark gray to true black, fine-grained aphanitic texture, hand-dressed rough-faced ashlar; occasional olivine phenocrysts as lighter-green specks; laid in regular courses with thin (10-15mm) light-gray lime mortar.
stone_basalt_volcanic_mena.region_notes: Hauran (Southern Syria/Northern Jordan), Jebel Druze, Yemeni highlands, Harrat volcanic fields.
stone_basalt_volcanic_mena.vlm_scoring_notes: Black-basalt + white-lime-mortar contrast is a strong unambiguous visual signature.
stone_basalt_volcanic_mena.substrate_finish_source: Cleft, riven or flamed stone surface.

stone_coral_cut.vhc_source: Farid et al. 2020 Energy & Buildings 213:109826 DOI:10.1016/j.enbuild.2020.109826 (Zanzibar coral stone rho 1200-1600 midpoint 1400, lambda 0.4-0.7). cp~840 from ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Limestone' (primary anchor). rho=1400,cp=840 -> 1176.
stone_coral_cut.porosity_notes: Farid et al. 2020 Hg-porosimetry 35-55%; UNESCO Zanzibar Stone Town technical documentation confirms range; ASTM C97 water absorption 15-30%.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 (cream/pale limestone SR 0.45-0.55); Levinson et al. 2010 Energy & Buildings 42(9):1615.

stone_coral_cut.visual_descriptors: Cream-white to pale buff-yellow; visible macro-pores and preserved branching coral skeletal texture on cut faces; often overlaid with lime-plaster that weathers away to reveal coral body.
stone_coral_cut.region_notes: Coastal Arabia, East African Swahili coast (Zanzibar, Lamu, Mombasa), Maldives, Caribbean.
stone_coral_cut.substrate_finish_source: Cleft, riven or flamed stone surface.

stone_flagstone.vhc_source: EnergyPlus 'Quartzitic and sandstone - 2240 kg/m3 - 13mm' rho=2240,cp=840; ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Quartzitic and sandstone, 140 lb/ft3'
stone_flagstone.porosity_notes: Sandstone/limestone flagstones commonly 10-25% per USGS and BS EN 12407; water absorption 3-8% by mass.

solar_reflectance.source: LBNL Heat Island Group pavement albedo dataset — sandstone/flagstone SR 0.25-0.35.

stone_flagstone.visual_descriptors: Irregular or rectilinear slabs 20-60mm thick with natural cleft surface; warm buff/tan/ochre tones; mortared or dry-laid with sand-filled joints; visible bedding and occasional ripple marks.
stone_flagstone.region_notes: US sandstone rho=2200-2400; UK York stone rho=2350-2500, lower porosity (~8%); Indian Kota rho=2500-2700, low porosity, greenish; Mediterranean travertine rho=2300-2500 with voids >15% POROUS.
stone_flagstone.substrate_finish_source: Cleft, riven or flamed stone surface.

stone_granite.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Calcitic, dolomitic, limestone, marble, and granite, 160 lb/ft3' rho=2563,cp=795
stone_granite.porosity_notes: USGS Bulletin 1144-E effective porosity 0.4-1.5% (<2% threshold); ASTM C97 water absorption <=0.4%.

solar_reflectance.source: LBNL Heat Island Group data + Doulos, Santamouris & Livada 2004 Solar Energy 77:231 — polished gray granite SR ~0.20; flamed/honed SR 0.25-0.30.

stone_granite.visual_descriptors: Coarse speckled crystalline pattern of quartz, feldspar and mica in gray/pink/black; surface typically polished-mirror or honed-matte with sharp sawn edges and minimal veining.

substrate_finish_alternate.note: Alternate as-manufactured state. Switch here if the project context differs.

stone_granite.substrate_finish_source: TOGGLED: honed taken as default, being more common than polished in residential flooring and cladding.

stone_limestone.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Limestone, 150 lb/ft3' rho=2403,cp=837 (Kumaran 2002)
stone_limestone.porosity_notes: Sedimentary carbonate; USGS data and ASTM C568 Type I-III give 5-25% porosity — spans semi-porous to porous depending on density class.

solar_reflectance.source: HDG Building Materials SRI primer citing ASTM E903 measurements on Indiana limestone SR ~0.43; Doulos et al. 2004.

stone_limestone.visual_descriptors: Fine to medium grain cream/buff/gray sedimentary stone with occasional fossil inclusions; honed matte or sawn finish; visible bedding planes; subtle mottling.
stone_limestone.region_notes: Indiana limestone (ASTM C568 Type II, rho=2300-2400, 12-20% porosity) -> porous band. Indian Kota stone (Type III, rho=2500-2700, <2%) -> non-porous, thermal mass ~2150.
stone_limestone.substrate_finish_source: Honed. Soft stone rarely takes a full polish.

stone_marble.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Calcitic, dolomitic, limestone, marble, and granite, 160 lb/ft3' rho=2563,cp=795 (same row covers marble)
stone_marble.porosity_notes: Metamorphic calcite/dolomite; USGS and ASTM C503 give 0.5-2% water absorption — within non-porous band.

solar_reflectance.source: Doulos, Santamouris & Livada 2004 Solar Energy 77:231 — polished white marble SR ~0.55 (Carrara-type).

stone_marble.visual_descriptors: Flowing vein patterns (gray/gold/green) on white to cream ground; high mirror polish producing specular reflections; cut slabs bookmatched at panel joints.
stone_marble.vlm_scoring_notes: Dark marbles (nero marquina, emperador) drop SR into matte band ~0.10-0.25 — color-specific adjustment required.

substrate_finish_alternate.note: Alternate as-manufactured state. Switch here if the project context differs.

stone_marble.substrate_finish_source: TOGGLED: honed taken as default for the same reason.

stone_slate.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 33 Table 3 'Properties of Solids' solid slate rho=2770,cp=760. NOTE: EnergyPlus 'F14 Slate or tile' cp=1260 reflects mortared assembly and OVERSTATES solid-stone cp.
stone_slate.porosity_notes: USGS data; metamorphic pelite 0.4-2% water absorption per ASTM C121 — non-porous.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 — dark slate SR 0.08-0.15.

stone_slate.visual_descriptors: Dark blue-gray to black cleft face with natural fissility; irregular layered edges; subtle sheen catching raking light; random-width graduated courses on roofs.
stone_slate.substrate_finish_source: Cleft, riven or flamed stone surface.

straw_bale.vhc_source: Tlaiji et al. 2022 Energies 15(21):7859 DOI:10.3390/en15217859 (rho 80-120, cp 1500-1800, lambda 0.033-0.19). rho=100,cp=1800 -> 180. ASTM E2392; California App. R.

level2_areal.note: Interior lime/earth render adds 20-40mm mineral skin supplying usable thermal mass; bale core itself contributes negligible mass.

straw_bale.porosity_notes: Inter-stem void fraction ~90% per Tlaiji et al. 2022; ASTM E2392/E2392M-10e1.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 (fresh lime plaster on straw bale SR 0.50-0.65); EPA Cool Pavements Compendium 2012 S4.

straw_bale.visual_descriptors: When finished: thick (450-600mm) wall with deep window reveals showing bale profile; slightly undulating lime-plastered exterior; cream/off-white color.
straw_bale.substrate_finish_note: Fibrous, loose or non-planar surface. Does not present a specular gloss class under ISO 2813.

tadelakt.vhc_source: Lanas & Alvarez 2003 Cem. Concr. Res. 33(11):1867 DOI:10.1016/S0008-8846(03)00217-3 (polished lime plaster rho~1820, lambda 0.85). Assael et al. 2010 Int. J. Thermophys. 31:844 (cp~920). Johansson et al. 2016 J. Cultural Heritage 22:978. rho=1820,cp=900 -> 1638.

level2_areal.note: Applied 3-8mm over existing render substrate — thin finish layer. Total wall mass depends on substrate.

tadelakt.porosity_notes: Burnishing + olive-oil soap (calcium stearate) reduces surface porosity to <2% per Johansson et al. 2016 JCH 22:978. Bulk matrix porosity 15-22% but surface-sealed.

solar_reflectance.source: Lanas & Alvarez 2003 CCR 33:1867 and Johansson et al. 2016 JCH 22:978 (high-burnish lime surface SR 0.62 for light lime shade; ochre ~0.35; deep red ~0.22).

tadelakt.visual_descriptors: High-polish waxy sheen; seamless monolithic surface without joints; earth-tone pigments (ochre, terracotta, deep red, saffron) common; slight undulations from hand-burnishing.
tadelakt.vlm_scoring_notes: Sheen + pigmented earth-tone monolithic surface is diagnostic. SR 0.62 at semi-gloss/gloss boundary — accept either.
tadelakt.substrate_finish_source: Stone-burnished and soaped; burnishing is integral to manufacture. The only plaster in the catalogue that is not matte.

tatami_mat.vhc_source: JIS A 5902:2019 Tatami-Doko. Ranjith et al. 2023 CBM (rice-straw cp 1.3-3.2 J/gK; straw-core doko rho 130-170). Tanaka et al. 2006 ASHRAE Transactions 112(1) (rho*cp composite 300-380). rho=150,cp=2250 -> 340.
tatami_mat.porosity_notes: Compressed rice-straw core void fraction 65-78% per JIS A 5902:2019 S5; igusa rush adds 20-30% additional void.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 (pale cellulosic surface). Weathered tatami drops to SR~0.30.

tatami_mat.visual_descriptors: Rectangular mats in standard Japanese modules; pale green-yellow when new -> golden-honey with age; fine parallel weave texture; characteristic dark indigo or black fabric edge binding (heri) 20-40mm wide.
tatami_mat.region_notes: Japan dominant; some Korea, Taiwan historic use.
tatami_mat.vlm_scoring_notes: Edge binding (heri) is the unambiguous VLM signal.
tatami_mat.substrate_finish_note: Fibrous, loose or non-planar surface. Does not present a specular gloss class under ISO 2813.

terrazzo_floor.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Calcitic/dolomitic/limestone/marble/granite' (rho=2563,cp=795) as aggregate; 'Cement plaster' (rho=1860,cp=840) as matrix. 70% aggregate + 30% cement: rho~2350,cp~810 -> 1900. Typical installed rho~2200,cp~800 -> 1800. NTMA technical data.
terrazzo_floor.porosity_notes: Ground and polished surface + sealer reduces open porosity to <1% per ASTM C413; epoxy-matrix terrazzo effectively zero. NTMA spec S2.06.

solar_reflectance.source: Levinson et al. 2011 LBNL Cool Floors (polished terrazzo SR 0.50-0.65); Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1.

terrazzo_floor.visual_descriptors: Smooth high-polish flat surface with visible speckled distribution of 5-15mm angular marble/granite chips in lighter cement or epoxy matrix; divider strips (brass/zinc) at 1.5-3m intervals; sheen reflects overhead lighting.
terrazzo_floor.substrate_finish_source: Ground and polished. Varies point to point across aggregate and matrix.
terrazzo_floor.substrate_finish_contested_note: Range 60-90 GU straddles the 70 GU edge and varies point to point across aggregate and matrix.

substrate_finish_alternate.note: Alternate as-manufactured state. Switch here if the project context differs.

thatch.vhc_source: CIBSE Guide A 2015 Table 3.12 (reed lambda=0.09, straw lambda=0.07 W/mK). Dimitrijeva-Kajaca & Iljins 2011 Latvian J. Physics 48(3):40 DOI:10.2478/v10047-011-0019-4 (rho 150-250, cp~1400). rho=200,cp=1400 -> 280.

level2_areal.note: 250-450mm thickness provides significant total thermal capacity per unit area despite low volumetric value.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 (dry vegetative matter range). New golden-brown ~0.35; weathered gray ~0.15-0.20.

thatch.visual_descriptors: Steep-pitched roof (45-55deg) with thick textured layer; golden-honey color when new, darkening to silver-gray with age; fine parallel stem texture; rounded ridge cap.
thatch.substrate_finish_note: Fibrous, loose or non-planar surface. Does not present a specular gloss class under ISO 2813.

thermally_modified_wood.vhc_source: Borrega & Karenlampi 2008 Holz als Roh- und Werkstoff 66(3):173 DOI:10.1007/s00107-007-0221-x (post-treatment rho=380-450, cp reduced ~5% from parent 1630 to ~1550). ETA-12/0074 Thermowood. ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Softwoods' parent baseline. rho=400,cp=1550 -> 620.
thermally_modified_wood.porosity_notes: Thermal modification closes part of cell-wall pore network, reduces EMC 40-50%; EN 927-4 and Nordtest NT BUILD 491 show water absorption 6-12% by mass -> 8-12% volumetric (semi-porous band).

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 (dark-medium brown wood SR 0.15-0.28).

thermally_modified_wood.visual_descriptors: Uniform rich chocolate-brown to mahogany color with markedly reduced grain contrast; smooth planed or lightly textured surface; usually installed as exterior cladding in shiplap, board-and-batten, or open-rainscreen patterns with shadow-gap joints.
thermally_modified_wood.region_notes: Strongly associated with Nordic and Central European contemporary architecture.
thermally_modified_wood.vlm_scoring_notes: Key diagnostic vs naturally weathered wood: UNIFORM dark brown without silver-gray UV-weathering patina. Do not default to 'aged/weathered wood'.
thermally_modified_wood.substrate_finish_source: Sawn or planed timber, unfinished. Category range for raw substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

timber_decking.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Softwoods — Southern yellow pine' rho=497,cp=1633 (Kumaran 2002) as proxy for pressure-treated pine.
timber_decking.porosity_notes: Softwood tracheid structure ~65% void fraction; pressure-treatment (ACQ, MCA) occupies only cell-wall substance, reducing porosity slightly to ~60%.

solar_reflectance.source: HDG Building Materials/Dasso.XTR data — weathered wood decking SR ~0.25; new treated pine SR ~0.40.

timber_decking.visual_descriptors: Parallel planks 20-30mm thick with visible grain; fastener heads at joist bays; checking and silver-gray patina with UV exposure; gaps 5-8mm between boards for drainage.
timber_decking.region_notes: Western Red Cedar rho~380 -> LOW thermal mass (~620). Tropical hardwoods (Ipe, Cumaru) rho~1050,cp~1700 -> HIGH thermal mass (~1785). Regional species shift class.
timber_decking.vlm_scoring_notes: Very dark oiled tropical hardwood looks like composite decking — grain run and fastener pattern distinguish.
timber_decking.substrate_finish_source: Sawn or planed timber, unfinished. Category range for raw substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

tropical_hardwood_ipe.vhc_source: USDA FPL Wood Handbook FPL-GTR-190 2010 Table 4-3a (Handroanthus spp. rho=1010-1130 at 12% MC; midpoint 1070). ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Hardwoods' row (cp~1700 per Wilkes 1979). rho=1070,cp=1700 -> 1819.
tropical_hardwood_ipe.porosity_notes: USDA FPL-GTR-190 Ch 4 (Ipe basic SG 0.92-1.00; ASTM D4442 surface absorption <2%).

solar_reflectance.source: Doulos et al. 2004 Solar Energy 77(2):231 DOI:10.1016/j.solener.2004.04.006 (dark wood SR 0.15-0.22); Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1.

tropical_hardwood_ipe.visual_descriptors: Dark chocolate-brown to olive-brown, tight straight grain, oiled semi-gloss sheen when new matting to silver-gray when weathered.
tropical_hardwood_ipe.vlm_scoring_notes: Silvered weathered Ipe can be confused with weathered teak or cedar — disambiguate via fine tight grain and board flatness.
tropical_hardwood_ipe.mpcat40_note: 38 (otherstructure) for decking/cladding; floor applications may map to 2.
tropical_hardwood_ipe.substrate_finish_source: Sawn or planed timber, unfinished. Category range for raw substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

tropical_hardwood_merbau.vhc_source: USDA FPL Wood Handbook FPL-GTR-190 2010 Table 4-3a (Intsia bijuga rho=800-900 at 12% MC; midpoint 850). ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Hardwoods' row (cp~1700). rho=850,cp=1700 -> 1445.
tropical_hardwood_merbau.porosity_notes: USDA FPL-GTR-190 Ch 4 + ISO 10456:2007; Merbau 24h water absorption ~8-12% by mass (ASTM D4442).

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 (dark-medium wood SR 0.18-0.26); Doulos et al. 2004 Solar Energy 77:231.

tropical_hardwood_merbau.visual_descriptors: Deep red-brown to orange-brown heartwood with yellow flecks (sulphur deposits) in pores; interlocked grain producing ribbon figure on quartersawn faces; characteristic tannin-bleed staining.
tropical_hardwood_merbau.vlm_scoring_notes: Yellow pore-fleck deposits are strong visual discriminator from Ipe (no yellow flecks).
tropical_hardwood_merbau.substrate_finish_source: Sawn or planed timber, unfinished. Category range for raw substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

tropical_hardwood_teak.vhc_source: USDA FPL Wood Handbook FPL-GTR-190 2010 Table 4-3a (Tectona grandis rho=630-720 at 12% MC; midpoint 675). ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Hardwoods' row (cp=1630 per Wilkes 1979). rho=675,cp=1630 -> 1100.
tropical_hardwood_teak.porosity_notes: USDA FPL-GTR-190 Ch 4 (teak SG 0.55; ASTM D4442 24h absorption 6-9% by mass).

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 (medium-tone wood SR 0.30-0.40).

tropical_hardwood_teak.visual_descriptors: Golden-honey to medium warm brown with darker streaks, straight to slightly wavy grain, oily lustrous surface when freshly oiled; silvers to pale gray when unfinished and weathered.
tropical_hardwood_teak.substrate_finish_source: Sawn or planed timber, unfinished. Category range for raw substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

uk_dense_engineering_brick.vhc_source: BS 3921:1985 S6-7 (Class A >=70 N/mm2, <=4.5% boil absorption). CIBSE Guide A 2015 Table 3.49 (dense clay brick rho=2100, lambda=1.2, cp=800) -> 1680. Hammond & Jones ICE Inventory v2.0 (cp=800, rho 2050-2400). ISO 10456:2007.
uk_dense_engineering_brick.porosity_notes: Water absorption <=4.5% by mass (boil test BS 3921:1985 S7.2); open porosity ~9% by volume BUT classified non-porous per BS engineering-brick performance convention; semi-vitreous fired body. BS EN 772-7:1998 applicable.
uk_dense_engineering_brick.porosity_criterion_override: Water absorption <=4.5% by mass (boil test BS 3921:1985 S7.2); open porosity ~9% by volume BUT classified non-porous per BS engineering-brick performance convention; semi-vitreous fired body. BS EN 772-7:1998 applicable.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 (dark-red brick 0.20-0.30; dark-blue brick <0.10). Staffordshire blue SR~0.08; Accrington red SR~0.22. Value 0.14 is mid-range.

uk_dense_engineering_brick.visual_descriptors: Sharp-edged precise rectangular units (215x102.5x65mm UK format); vitreous semi-gloss face sheen; deep colors — Staffordshire blue (near-black) or Accrington red (deep red-brown); very tight mortar joints; high-frequency surface texture; engineering Flemish or English bond.
uk_dense_engineering_brick.region_notes: UK, Ireland primary. Staffordshire blue from Etruria Marl clays; Accrington red from Lancashire Nori brick.
uk_dense_engineering_brick.vlm_scoring_notes: Key discriminator from common facing brick: much darker color, vitreous face sheen, specific structural contexts.
uk_dense_engineering_brick.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

vinyl_lvt_linoleum.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Linoleum/cork tile, 1/4 in.' rho=465,cp~1593 (Kumaran 2002); ISO 10456/EN ISO 24011.

level2_areal.note: Installed at 2-5mm -> areal mass 1.5-3.7 kJ/m2K, effective class LOW.

vinyl_lvt_linoleum.porosity_notes: Sheet vinyl/LVT <1% (impervious); linoleum (oxidized linseed oil + cork flour) 5-10% open porosity per EN ISO 24011.

solar_reflectance.source: IES Lighting Handbook — commercial resilient flooring luminous reflectance ~0.25 used as SR proxy.

vinyl_lvt_linoleum.visual_descriptors: Smooth resilient sheet with printed wood, stone or solid-color pattern; low-profile welded seams on sheet vinyl; click-lock joints on LVT; satin wear-layer sheen.
vinyl_lvt_linoleum.substrate_finish_source: Matte wear layer is the current default; satin variants 15-30 GU.

vinyl_siding.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Polyvinyl chloride (PVC)' (rho=1380,cp=900 -> 1242). ISO 10456:2007 polymers row. ASTM D3679.

level2_areal.note: Panel face ~1.1mm thick with hollow-back air cavity; effective per-area mass ~1.4 kJ/m2K — negligible.

vinyl_siding.porosity_notes: Extruded PVC <0.5% closed porosity per ASTM D3679 S6.

solar_reflectance.source: CRRC Rated Products Directory vinyl/PVC siding listings (white SR 0.68-0.78, tan/beige 0.30-0.45, dark 0.08-0.18); LBNL LBNL-61498 Cool Colors project.

vinyl_siding.visual_descriptors: Horizontal lapped siding profile (Dutchlap, clapboard) in consistent planks 100-200mm exposure; slight texture simulating wood grain; hollow-back cavity visible at cut ends; gentle semi-gloss sheen.
vinyl_siding.region_notes: Dominant US/Canadian residential cladding (~30% market share); less common in Europe, Australia, Asia.
vinyl_siding.substrate_finish_source: Deliberately low-gloss. Note: siding is measured at 75deg per ASTM D523/D2457, not 60deg.
vinyl_siding.substrate_finish_method: ASTM D2457 at 75 degrees (siding geometry), NOT ISO 2813 at 60 degrees
vinyl_siding.substrate_finish_contested_note: Measured at 75deg per ASTM D2457, so the value is not directly comparable with the 60deg band boundaries used elsewhere in this dimension.

volcanic_pumice_concrete.vhc_source: ISO 10456:2007 Table 3 'Lightweight aggregate concrete' (rho 800-1800, lambda 0.30-1.15, cp=1000). Demirbogas & Gul 2003 Cem. Concr. Res. 33(5):723 DOI:10.1016/S0008-8846(02)01032-3 (lambda 0.20-0.35, density reduction ~40%). rho=1300,cp=1000 -> 1300. EN 206:2013+A2.
volcanic_pumice_concrete.porosity_notes: Total porosity 22-38% per EN 1936:2006 and Demirbogas & Gul 2003; pumice aggregate intrinsic vesicular porosity 65-85%. ASTM C330.

solar_reflectance.source: Levinson et al. 2010 LBNL-2007E (light-gray concrete 0.30-0.45); Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1.

volcanic_pumice_concrete.visual_descriptors: Pale gray concrete matrix with distinctive dark-gray to black vesicular pumice aggregate (8-20mm porous dark inclusions); matte to slightly rough surface.
volcanic_pumice_concrete.region_notes: Iceland, Italy (Lipari/Campania), Japan (Shirasu), Turkey (Central Anatolia), Greece (Santorini).
volcanic_pumice_concrete.substrate_finish_source: Raw mineral/earthen surface; diffuse scattering. Category range for uncoated substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

water_surface.vhc_source: ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 33 Table 3 water at 25C rho=997,cp=4186 — highest thermal mass of any common building material.
water_surface.porosity_notes: Bulk fluid; classified non-porous by convention for solar/surface modeling.
water_surface.porosity_criterion_override: Bulk fluid; classified non-porous by convention for solar/surface modeling.

solar_reflectance.source: Oke Boundary Layer Climates Table 1.1 — calm water high-sun SR 0.03-0.10.

water_surface.visual_descriptors: Specular reflective surface with sky/mirror reflections; ripple and wave patterns; transparency revealing pool finish or lake-bed near edges; chlorination haze or natural color variation.
water_surface.vlm_scoring_notes: Solar reflectance is highly angle-dependent; low-sun albedo can exceed 0.5 (Fresnel). Default 0.07 applies for overhead-sun convention.
water_surface.substrate_finish_note: Fibrous, loose or non-planar surface. Does not present a specular gloss class under ISO 2813.

wood_fiber_insulation_board.vhc_source: Latif et al. 2014 Energy & Buildings 82:561 DOI:10.1016/j.enbuild.2014.07.047 (rho=200 nominal mid-range, cp=2100, lambda=0.042). WUFI IBP 'Holzfaserdammplatte' / 'Wood Fiber Board (Pavatex)' entry confirms. EN 13171:2012+A1:2015. rho=200,cp=2100 -> 420.

level2_areal.note: 420 kJ/m3K is technically LOW (<500 threshold) despite being ~12x higher than mineral wool. Denser grades (rho=260-270) reach 546 kJ/m3K -> MEDIUM.

wood_fiber_insulation_board.porosity_notes: Open porosity >85% per Latif et al. 2014 helium pycnometry; hygroscopic sorption 8-18% across 33-93% RH per EN ISO 12571:2013.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 (natural tan/beige cellulose-fiber surface SR 0.30-0.45).

wood_fiber_insulation_board.visual_descriptors: Rigid compressed-fiber boards with visible randomly oriented wood fiber texture; uniform tan-beige to light brown; matte-to-semi-gloss slightly fuzzy surface; factory-cut sharp edges; typical thickness 20-240mm.
wood_fiber_insulation_board.region_notes: Dominant in German-speaking Alpine, Nordic, and French eco-construction; much rarer in UK, North America, East Asia.
wood_fiber_insulation_board.vlm_scoring_notes: Boundary case: 420 sits 16% below 500 threshold. Denser grades cross into MEDIUM.
wood_fiber_insulation_board.substrate_finish_source: Sawn or planed timber, unfinished. Category range for raw substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

woven_bamboo_panel.vhc_source: Nurdiah 2016 Procedia Social and Behavioral Sciences 234:985 DOI:10.1016/j.sbspro.2016.10.285 (woven bamboo panel lambda~0.20, rho=400-600; midpoint 500). Shah et al. 2016 J. Mater. Sci. 51(6):2991 (bamboo cp 1700-1800; midpoint 1750). rho=500,cp=1750 -> 875.

level2_areal.note: Open-weave panel with >40% void fraction delivers ~60% of nominal rho*cp at envelope level. Thermally functions closer to LOW mass.

woven_bamboo_panel.porosity_notes: ISO 22157:2019 bamboo vessel structure; open-weave adds 30-50% macro-porosity on top of ~40-55% intrinsic culm porosity.

solar_reflectance.source: Berdahl & Bretz 1997 Energy & Buildings 25:149 DOI:10.1016/S0378-7788(96)01004-1 (light natural wood/bamboo SR 0.35-0.45).

woven_bamboo_panel.visual_descriptors: Warm straw-tan to golden beige; strongly geometric plain or twill weave pattern (10-30mm splint width); visible node bands; darkens to deep amber-brown with age.
woven_bamboo_panel.substrate_finish_source: Sawn or planed timber, unfinished. Category range for raw substrates ~0-8 GU (ISO 2813 60deg).

zellige_mosaic_tile.vhc_source: Garcia et al. 2011 J. European Ceramic Society 31(8):1359 DOI:10.1016/j.jeurceramsoc.2011.01.018 (ceramic rho 1900-2100 midpoint 2000, cp~840). ISO 13006:2018 ceramic tile. ASHRAE HOF 2021 Ch 26 Table 1 'Clay tile' cross-check. rho=2000,cp=840 -> 1680.
zellige_mosaic_tile.porosity_notes: ISO 13006:2018 Group AIIb/BIIb water absorption 6-10% by mass -> ~12-18% vol; surface glaze seals face to effective <1%.

solar_reflectance.source: CRRC Rated Products Directory glazed clay tile (SR 0.30-0.65 color-dependent); Levinson et al. 2010 Energy & Buildings 42(9):1615 DOI:10.1016/j.enbuild.2010.05.004 cool colored tiles; Berdahl & Bretz 1997.

zellige_mosaic_tile.visual_descriptors: Hand-cut geometric tesserae (10-40mm) in complex star-and-polygon patterns; vivid saturated glazes (cobalt blue, emerald green, ochre yellow, white, black); always mirror-gloss specular surface.
zellige_mosaic_tile.region_notes: Morocco (Fez primary production), Al-Andalus, Algeria, Tunisia.
zellige_mosaic_tile.vlm_scoring_notes: SR 0.45 = semi-gloss radiometric but visual appearance is high-gloss specular. White-dominant patterns: SR 0.65 (true gloss). Cobalt/black-dominant: SR 0.25 (matte).
zellige_mosaic_tile.substrate_finish_source: Traditional glossy glaze. Zellige is hand-glazed and varies point to point.
zellige_mosaic_tile.substrate_finish_contested_note: Range 40-90 GU spans two bands and varies point to point on a hand-glazed surface.
